楊播楊敷
Yang Bo and Yang Fu

列傳第二十九
Biographies 29
3
楊播子侃播弟椿椿子昱椿弟津津子遁逸謐謐弟愔燕子獻鄭頤楊敷子素孫玄感素弟約約從叔異敷叔父寬寬子文恩紀
Yang Bo's son Kan; Bo's younger brother Chun; Chun's son Yu; Chun's younger brother Jin; Jin's sons Dun, Yi, and Mi; Mi's younger brother Yin; Yanzi Xian; Zheng Yi; Yang Fu's son Su; Su's grandson Xuan'gan; Su's younger brother Yue; Yue's father's younger cousin Yi; Fu's uncle Kuan; Kuan's sons Wen, En, and Ji
4
楊播，字延慶，弘農華陰人也。 高祖結，仕慕容氏，位中山相。 曾祖珍，道武時歸國，位上谷太守。 祖真，河內、清河二郡太守。 父懿，延興末為廣平太守，有稱績。 孝文南巡，吏人頌之，徵為選部給事中，有公平譽。 除安南將軍、洛州刺史，未之任，卒。 贈本官，加弘農公，諡曰簡。
Yang Bo, whose style name was Yanqing, came from Huayin in Hongnong commandery. His great-grandfather Jie had served the Murong and risen to chancellor of Zhongshan. His great-grandfather Zhen submitted to the Wei in the reign of Emperor Daowu and was appointed administrator of Shanggu. His grandfather Zhen had been administrator of both Henei and Qinghe. His father Yi, late in the Yanxing era, served as administrator of Guangping and earned a name for solid performance. When Emperor Wen made his southern tour, local officials and commoners praised Yi; he was recalled to the Selection Bureau as an attendant-in-ordinary and won renown for impartiality. He was appointed general who pacifies the south and inspector of Luozhou, but died before he could assume the post. He was posthumously granted his former rank, ennobled as Duke of Hongnong, and given the posthumous name Jian (Plain).
5
播本字元休，孝文賜改焉。 母王氏，文明太后之外姑。 播少修飭，奉養盡禮。 擢為中散，累遷衛尉少卿。 與陽平王頤等出漠北擊蠕蠕，大致克獲。 遷武衛將軍，復征蠕蠕，至居然山而還。 及車駕南討，假前將軍，從至鐘離。 師回，詔播為圓陣禦之。 相拒再宿，軍人食盡，賊圍更急。 播乃領精騎三百，曆其船大呼曰：「我今欲度，能戰者出。 」遂擁而濟，賊莫敢動。 賜爵華陰子。 後從駕討破崔慧景、蕭愆于鄧城，進號平東將軍。 時車駕耀威城沔水，上巳設宴，帝與中軍彭城王勰賭射，左衛元遙在勰朋內，而播居帝曹。 遙射侯正中，籌限已滿。 帝曰：「左衛籌足，右衛不得不解。 」對曰：「仰恃聖恩，庶幾必爭」，於是箭正中。 帝笑曰：「雖養由之妙，何復過是。 」遂舉卮以賜播曰：「古人酒以養病，朕今賞卿之能，可謂古今殊也。 」除太府卿，進爵為伯。
Bo had originally been styled Yuanxiu; Emperor Wen granted him the new style name Yanqing. His mother, of the Wang clan, was a maternal aunt by marriage of Empress Dowager Wenming. From youth Bo cultivated propriety and observed every duty in caring for his parents. He was promoted to palace attendant and rose in stages to vice director of the court of the imperial clan. He joined the Prince of Yangping, Yi, and others on a campaign north of the desert against the Rouran and won substantial booty. He was made general of the martial guard, campaigned again against the Rouran, reached Mount Juran, and withdrew. When the emperor marched south on campaign, Bo was given acting rank as forward general and accompanied the host to Zhongli. On the army's withdrawal, an edict ordered Bo to form a circular formation and hold the enemy at bay. They stood opposed for two nights; the troops ran out of food while the enemy ring drew tighter. Bo then led three hundred picked horsemen along the line of enemy boats and shouted, "I am crossing now—whoever means to fight, come out!" " He pressed through and crossed; not one of the enemy dared move against him. He was granted the title Viscount of Huayin. Later he accompanied the emperor in the defeat of Cui Huijing and Xiao Yi at Dengcheng and was promoted to general who pacifies the east. The emperor was then displaying his might at the Han River fortress. On the Shangsi festival a banquet was held; the emperor and the central army commander, the Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, wagered at archery. Yuan Yao of the left guard stood in Xie's party while Bo stood in the emperor's. Yao's arrow struck the target dead center, filling the allotted tally. The emperor said, "The left guard's tally is full—the right guard has no choice but to concede." " Bo replied, "Trusting in Your Majesty's grace, I shall surely contend," and his arrow likewise struck dead center. The emperor laughed and said, "Yang Youbu's skill was legendary, yet how could it surpass this?" " He raised a goblet and presented it to Bo, saying, "The ancients drank wine to nurse illness; I now reward your prowess—a gift past and present could scarcely match." " He was appointed director of the imperial treasury and advanced to marquis.
6
後為華州刺史。 至州，借人田，為御史王基所劾，除官爵，卒於家。 子侃等停柩不葬，披訴積年。 至熙平中，乃贈鎮西將軍、雍州刺史，並復其爵，諡曰壯。
He was later made inspector of Huazhou. After taking up his post he borrowed peasants' fields; the censor Wang Ji impeached him, he was stripped of office and rank, and died at home. His son Kan and others refused to bury the coffin and petitioned for redress year after year. In the Xiping era he was posthumously made general who guards the west and inspector of Yongzhou; his title was restored and he was given the posthumous name Zhuang (Stalwart).
7
侃字士業，頗愛琴書，尤好計畫。 時播一門，貴滿朝廷，子侄早通，而侃獨不交遊，公卿罕有識者。 親朋勸其出仕，侃曰：「苟有良田，何憂晚歲，但恨無才具耳。 」年三十一，襲爵華陰伯。
Kan, styled Shiye, was devoted to music and books and had a particular gift for strategy. Bo's whole clan then filled the court with rank; sons and nephews won early preferment, yet Kan kept to himself and few grandees even knew his name. Relatives urged him to enter service; Kan replied, "With good land in hand, why fret over one's later years? I only regret lacking the talent for it." " At thirty-one he succeeded to the marquisate of Huayin.
8
揚州刺史長孫承業請為錄事參軍。 梁豫州刺史裴邃規相掩襲，密購壽春人李瓜花、袁建等令為內應。 邃已纂勒兵士，慮壽春疑覺，遂謬移云：「魏始於馬頭置戍，如聞復欲修白捺舊城。 若爾，便稍相侵逼。 此亦須營歐陽，設交境之備。 今板卒已集，唯聽信還。 」佐寮咸欲以實答之，雲無修白捺意。 而侃曰：「白捺小城，本非形勝，邃集兵遣移，虛構是言，得無有別圖也？ 」承業乃云：「錄事可造移報。 」移曰：「彼之纂兵，想別有意，何為妄構白捺？ 他人有心，予忖度之，勿謂秦無人也。 」邃得移，謂已覺，便散兵。 瓜花等以期契不會，便相告發，伏辜者十數家。 邃後竟襲襲壽春，入羅城而退，遂列營于黎漿、梁城，日夕鈔掠。 承業乃奏侃為統軍。
Zhangsun Chengye, inspector of Yangzhou, invited him to serve as recording secretary. Pei Sui, Liang's inspector of Yuzhou, plotted a surprise assault and secretly enlisted Li Guahua, Yuan Jian, and other men of Shouchun as inside agents. Sui had already mustered his troops but feared Shouchun would scent the plot; he therefore sent a deceptive dispatch claiming, "Wei has newly garrisoned Matou, and we hear they mean to repair the old fortress at Bainuo." If that is so, they will gradually press upon our borders. We too must fortify Ouyang and prepare defenses along the frontier. Labor and troops are already assembled; we await only your word to stand down. " The staff all wished to answer truthfully that Wei had no plan to repair Bainuo. Kan objected: "Bainuo is a minor post and no strategic prize. Sui has mustered troops and invented this pretext—can he have no deeper design?" " Chengye said, "Let the recording secretary draft our reply." " The dispatch ran: "Your mustering of troops surely serves another purpose—why invent a tale about Bainuo?" Others have their designs, and I have taken their measure; do not suppose that Qin has no wise men left. " Sui received the dispatch, concluded he had been found out, and disbanded his army. Guahua and the others, their rendezvous having failed, turned informer on one another; more than ten households paid with their lives. Sui later attacked Shouchun after all, breached the outer wall and withdrew, then encamped at Lijiang and Liangcheng and raided without cease. Chengye memorialized to appoint Kan commander-in-chief.
9
後雍州刺史蕭寶夤據州反，隨業討之，除侃為承業行台左丞。 軍次恆農，侃白承業曰：「今賊守潼關，全據形勝。 須北取蒲阪，飛棹西岸，置兵死地，人有鬥心，華州之圍，可不戰而解； 潼關之賊，必望風潰散。 諸處既平，長安自克。 愚計可錄，請為明公前驅。 」承業從之，令其子子產等領騎與侃于恆農北度，便據石錐壁。 乃班告曰：「今且停軍於此，以待步卒，兼觀人情向背。 若送降名者，各自還村，侯台軍舉三烽火，各亦應之，以明降款。 其無應烽，即是不降之村，理須殄戮。 」人遂傳相告報。 實未降者，亦詐舉烽，一宿之間，火光遍數百里內。 圍城之寇，不測所以，各自散歸。 長安平，侃頗有力焉。 建義初，除岐州刺史。 屬元顥內逼，詔行北中郎將。
When Xiao Baoyin, inspector of Yongzhou, rebelled and held the province, Kan joined Chengye's punitive campaign and was made left assistant on Chengye's field staff. The army halted at Hengnong; Kan told Chengye, "The rebels hold Tong Pass and command every advantage of terrain." We must take Puban to the north, send swift boats to the western bank, and plant troops where retreat is impossible so they fight with desperate resolve—the siege of Huazhou can then be lifted without a battle; the rebels at Tong Pass will scatter at the mere rumor of our approach. Once the outlying posts are pacified, Chang'an will fall of itself. This plan is sound; allow me to serve as your vanguard. " Chengye agreed and sent his son Zichan and others with cavalry to cross north of Hengnong with Kan; they at once seized the Stone Cone cliff. They then proclaimed, "We halt here for the moment to await the infantry and to see which way the people lean." Those who mean to surrender should return to their villages; when the imperial army raises three beacon fires, each village should answer in kind to signal submission. Any village that fails to answer is a village that has not submitted and must be destroyed. " Word spread from village to village. Even villages that had not truly submitted lit false beacons; within a single night fires blazed across hundreds of li. The besiegers, unable to fathom what was happening, broke up and withdrew. When Chang'an fell, Kan had contributed substantially to the victory. At the opening of the Jianyi era he was appointed inspector of Qizhou. When Yuan Hao pressed inward on the capital, an edict appointed him acting northern central commander.
10
孝莊徙河北，執侃手曰：「朕停卿蕃寄，移任此者，正為今日。 但卿尊卑百口，若隨朕行，所累處大。 卿可還洛，寄之後圖。 」侃曰：「寧可以臣微族，頓廢君臣之義。 」固求陪從。 除度支尚書，兼給事黃門侍郎，敷西縣公。 及車駕南還，顥令梁將陳慶之守北中城，自據南岸。 有夏州義士為顥守河中渚，乃密信通款，求破橋立效。 爾硃榮赴之。 及橋破，應接不果，皆為顥屠。 榮將為還計，欲更圖後舉。 侃曰：「若今即還，人情失望，未若召發人材，唯多縛筏，間以舟楫，沿河廣布。 令數百里中，皆為度勢，顥知防何處？ 一旦得度，必立大功。 」榮大笑從之。 於是爾硃兆等於馬渚諸楊南度，顥便南走。 車駕入都，侃解尚書，正黃門。 以濟河功，進爵濟北郡公，復除其長子師仲為秘書郎。
Emperor Xiaozhuang withdrew to Hebei, took Kan's hand, and said, "I kept you in a frontier post and moved you here precisely for this day." Yet your household, high and low together, numbers a hundred mouths; if you march with me, the burden on the army would be heavy. Return to Luoyang and trust to what may come afterward. " Kan replied, "How could my humble clan abruptly cast aside the bond between ruler and subject?" " He insisted on accompanying the emperor. He was appointed minister of revenue and concurrent attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fuxi county. When the emperor returned south, Hao ordered the Liang general Chen Qingzhi to hold the north-central fortress while he himself took the south bank. A loyalist of Xiazhou holding a mid-river islet for Hao sent a secret letter offering allegiance and proposing to break the bridge as proof of his loyalty. Erzhu Rong hurried to the crossing. When the bridge was broken the planned link-up failed, and Hao's men slaughtered them all. Rong was readying a withdrawal and meant to wait for a better moment. Kan urged, "If we withdraw now, men's hearts will fail. Better to summon labor and timber, bind rafts in great numbers, mix in boats, and spread the fleet widely along the river." Let the appearance of a crossing stretch for hundreds of li—how will Hao know where to defend? Once we cross somewhere, we are sure to win a great victory. " Rong laughed and took his advice. Erzhu Zhao and others then crossed south of the Zhuyang ford at Mazhu, and Hao fled south at once. When the emperor entered the capital, Kan was relieved of the ministry and confirmed as attendant of the yellow gate. For his merit in the river crossing he was advanced to Duke of Jibei commandery, and his eldest son Shizhong was again appointed secretary.
11
時所用錢，人多私鑄，稍就薄小，乃至風飄水浮，米斗幾直一千。 侃奏聽人與官並鑄五銖，使人樂為，而俗弊得改。 莊帝從之。 後除侍中，加衛將軍、右光祿大夫。
The currency then in circulation was largely privately cast, growing ever thinner and lighter until coins would drift in the wind and float on water; a dou of grain cost nearly a thousand cash. Kan memorialized to permit private persons and the government alike to cast wuzhu coins, so that people would willingly mint sound money and the debased custom might be corrected. Emperor Zhuang approved the proposal. He was later made palace attendant, with the added titles general of the guard and right grand master of splendid happiness.
12
莊帝將圖爾硃榮，侃與內弟李晞、城陽王徽、侍中李彧等咸預其謀。 爾硃兆入洛，侃時休沐，遂竄歸華陰。 普泰初，天光在關西，遣侃子婦父韋義遠招慰之，立盟許恕其罪。 侃從兄昱恐為家禍，令侃出應，假其食言，不過一人身沒，冀全百口。 侃赴之，為天光所害。 太昌初，贈車騎將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史。 子純陀襲。
When Emperor Zhuang plotted against Erzhu Rong, Kan joined his brother-in-law Li Xi, the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, the attendant-in-ordinary Li Yu, and others in the conspiracy. When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Kan was on leave and fled home to Huayin. Early in the Putai era, Tian Guang held the western passes and sent Kan's father-in-law Wei Yiyuan to summon and reassure him, swearing a covenant that promised pardon. Kan's cousin Yu feared ruin for the whole clan and urged him to answer the summons, wagering that even if Tian Guang broke his oath, at most one man would die while a hundred kinsmen might be spared. Kan went—and Tian Guang killed him. Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made general of the cavalry and chariots, with honors equal to the three excellencies, and inspector of Youzhou. His son Chuntuo succeeded him.
13
播弟椿。 椿字延壽，本字仲考，孝文賜改焉。 性寬謹。 為內給事，與兄播並侍禁闈。 後為中部法曹，折訟公正，孝文嘉之。 及文明太后崩，孝文五日不食。 椿諫曰：「聖人之禮，毀不滅性，從陛下欲自賢於萬代，其若宗廟何！ 」帝感其言，乃一進粥。 轉授宮輿曹少卿，加給事中，出為豫州刺史，再遷梁州刺史。
Bo's younger brother was Chun. Chun, styled Yanshou, had originally been named Zhongkao; Emperor Wen granted him the new style name. He was by nature generous and cautious. He served as inner attendant and, together with his elder brother Bo, attended within the inner palace. He later served in the central legal bureau, judging cases with impartiality; Emperor Wen commended him. When Empress Dowager Wenming died, Emperor Wen fasted for five days. Chun remonstrated: "The sages taught that mourning must not destroy one's vital nature. If Your Majesty wishes to outshine every age in virtue, what becomes of the ancestral temple?" " The emperor was moved and took a single bowl of gruel. He was made vice director of the imperial carriages bureau and attendant-in-ordinary, then sent out as inspector of Yuzhou and later transferred to inspector of Liangzhou.
14
初，武興王楊集始降于齊，自漢中而北，規復舊土。 椿貽書集始，開以利害。 集始執書對使者曰：「楊使君此書，除我心腹疾。 」遂來降。 尋以母老解還。 後兼太僕卿。
Earlier the Prince of Wuxing, Yang Jishi, had defected to Qi and marched north from Hanzhong, intending to recover his former territory. Chun wrote to Jishi, laying out the costs and benefits of his course. Jishi took the letter and told the envoy, "Commissioner Yang's letter has lifted the sickness from my heart." " He then submitted. Soon afterward, on account of his aged mother, he was relieved and returned home. He was later made concurrent director of the imperial stud.
15
秦州羌呂苟兒、涇州屠各陳瞻等反，詔椿為別將，隸安西將軍元麗討之。 賊守峽自固。 或謀伏兵斷其出入，待糧盡攻之。 或云斬山木，從火焚之。 椿曰：「並非計也。 賊深竄，正避死耳。 今宜勒三軍勿更侵掠，賊必謂見險不前，心輕我軍，然後掩其不備，可一舉而平。 」乃緩師。 賊果出掠，仍以軍中驢馬餌之。 銜枚夜襲，斬瞻傳首。 入正太僕卿。
When the Qiang Lü Gou'er of Qinzhou and the Tuge Chen Zhan of Jingzhou rebelled, an edict made Chun a separate commander under the general who pacifies the west, Yuan Li. The rebels held the gorge and dug in. Some urged ambushing the passes and waiting until their grain ran out before attacking. Others proposed felling the timber on the slopes and burning them out with fire. Chun said, "Neither plan will do." The rebels have burrowed deep; they are simply trying to stay alive. We should order the armies to cease raiding; the rebels will think we shrink from the terrain and grow contemptuous—then we can strike when they are unprepared and end the rebellion in a single blow. " The army slowed its advance. The rebels duly came out to raid, and the army again used its donkeys and horses as bait. They attacked by night with gags in their mouths, beheaded Zhan, and sent his head to headquarters. He entered the capital as full director of the imperial stud.
16
初，獻文世有蠕蠕萬餘戶降附，居於高平、薄骨律二鎮。 太和末叛走，唯有一千餘家。 太中大夫王通、高平鎮將郎育等求徙置淮北，防其後叛。 詔椿徙焉。 椿上書，以為裔不謀夏，夷不亂華，是以先朝居之荒服之間，正欲悅近來遠。 今新附者眾，若舊者見徙，新者必不安，愚謂不可。 時八坐不從，遂於濟州緣河居之。 及冀州元愉之難，果悉浮河赴賊，所在鈔掠，如椿所策。 後除朔州刺史。 在州為廷尉奏椿前為太僕卿，招引百姓，盜種牧田三百四十頃，依律處刑五歲。 尚書邢巒據正始別格，奏罪應除名，注籍盜門，同籍合門不仕。 宣武以親律既班，不宜雜用舊制，詔依斷，以贖論。 後除定州刺史。
In the reign of Emperor Xianwen, more than ten thousand Rouran households had submitted and been settled at the garrisons of Gaoping and Bogulu. Late in the Taihe era most rebelled and fled, leaving only a little more than a thousand households. Wang Tong, grand master of palace counsel, Lang Yu, commander of the Gaoping garrison, and others asked that the remnant be moved north of the Huai to forestall another rebellion. An edict ordered Chun to carry out the move. Chun memorialized that distant peoples do not plot against the central states and barbarians do not disturb the civilized realm; the former court had settled them on the frontier precisely to win those near and draw those far. Many have newly submitted; if the old settlers are moved, the newcomers will surely grow uneasy. I hold that the move is inadvisable. The eight ministers overruled him, and the settlers were placed along the river in Jizhou. When Yuan Yu rebelled in Jizhou, they all crossed the river by raft to join him and raided wherever they went, exactly as Chun had predicted. He was later made inspector of Shuozhou. While he held the province, the minister of justice reported that as director of the imperial stud Chun had induced commoners to illicitly farm three hundred forty qing of pasture; by law he merited five years' penal service. Minister Xing Luan, citing the separate statutes of the Zhengshi era, argued that the offense warranted removal from office, registration in the thieves' roll, and disqualification of the entire household from service. Emperor Xuanwu held that with the new kin statutes in force the old penalties should not apply; an edict confirmed the judgment but allowed redemption. He was later made inspector of Dingzhou.
17
自道武平中山，多置軍府，以相威攝。 凡有八軍，軍各配兵五千，食祿主帥軍各四十六人。 自中原稍定，八軍之兵漸割南戍，一軍兵才千餘，然主帥如故，費祿不少。 椿表罷四軍，減其主帥百八十四人。 椿在州，因修黑山道餘功，伐木私造佛寺，役兵，為御史所劾，除名。
Since Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, numerous military offices had been established to keep one another in check. There were eight armies in all, each with five thousand troops and forty-six salaried commanders. As the central plains grew settled, the eight armies were gradually stripped to garrison the south; each army mustered barely a thousand men, yet the full complement of commanders remained and salaries still ran high. Chun memorialized to abolish four armies and cut one hundred eighty-four commanders. While in the province Chun used surplus labor from the Heishan road project to fell timber and build a private Buddhist temple, impressing troops in the process; a censor impeached him and he was stripped of rank.
18

He rose in stages to inspector of Yongzhou and was advanced to general of the cavalry and chariots with honors equal to the three excellencies. He was soon made palace attendant and concurrent right vice director of the imperial secretariat, appointed to a field headquarters, and given command of the generals west of the passes. Stricken with a sudden illness, he repeatedly begged to be relieved; the throne agreed and appointed Xiao Baoyin in his place as inspector and field commander.

Chun returned home and met his son Yu, who was bound for the capital; he had Yu report that Xiao Baoyin's rewards and punishments were arbitrary and outside the statutes, and that he suspected disloyalty. Yu reported in person to Emperor Ming and Empress Dowager Ling; neither would heed the warning. When Baoyin ambushed and killed the attendant of the imperial clan Li Daoyuan, he still memorialized in self-defense, claiming he had been slandered by Chun and his sons.

建義元年，為司徒。 永安初，進位太保，加侍中，給後部鼓吹。 元顥入洛，椿子昱為顥禽。 又椿弟順、順子仲宣、兄子侃、弟子遁並從駕河內，為顥嫌疑。 以椿家世顯重，恐失人望，未及加罪。 時人助其憂，或勸椿攜家避禍。 椿曰：「吾內外百口，何處逃竄？ 正當坐任運耳。」
In the first year of Jianyi he was appointed minister of education. Early in the Yong'an era he was advanced to grand tutor, made palace attendant, and granted imperial music for his rear guard. When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Chun's son Yu was taken by Hao. Chun's younger brother Shun, Shun's son Zhongxuan, his nephew Kan, and his younger brother's son Dun had all accompanied the emperor to Henei and fell under Hao's suspicion. Because the Yang clan was too eminent to offend lightly, Hao feared losing popular support and did not punish them. Others shared his anxiety and urged Chun to flee with his household. Chun said, "Within and without, we number a hundred mouths—where could we flee?" We can only sit and leave it to fate."

莊帝還宮，椿上書頻請歸老，詔聽服侍中服，賜朝服一襲、八尺床帳、幾、杖，不朝，乘安車，駕駟馬，給扶，傳詔二人，仰所在郡縣四時以禮存問安否。 椿奉辭于華林園，帝下御座，執手流淚曰：「公先帝舊臣，實為元老。 但高尚其志，決意不留，既難相違，深用淒切。 」椿亦歔欷，欲拜，帝親執不聽。 賜以絹布，給羽林衛送。 群公百寮餞于城西張方橋，行路觀者莫不稱歎。 椿臨行，誡子孫曰：
When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Chun repeatedly begged to retire. An edict permitted him to wear attendant's robes, granted court dress, an eight-foot bed canopy, a table, and a staff, exempted him from court, allowed a comfort carriage drawn by four horses with bearers to assist him, and assigned two edict-bearers, charging his home commandery and county to inquire after his health each season. Chun took leave at the Hualin Garden. The emperor descended from the throne, took his hand in tears, and said, "You are an old minister of my predecessor—truly the elder statesman of the court." Yet you hold your principles high and are resolved to go; since I cannot keep you, my grief is profound." " Chun sobbed as well and moved to bow, but the emperor held him and would not permit it. He was granted silk and cloth, and the Feathered Forest guard escorted him home. The assembled lords and officials gave him a farewell at Zhangfang Bridge west of the city; every passerby who watched sighed in admiration. Before he departed, Chun admonished his sons and grandsons:

我家入魏之始，即為上客。 自爾至今，二千石方伯不絕，祿恤甚多。 於親姻知故吉凶之際，必厚加贈襚； 來往賓寮，必以酒肉飲食，故六姻朋友無憾焉。 國家初，丈夫好服彩色。 吾雖不記上谷翁時事，然記清河翁時服飾。 恆見翁著布衣韋帶，常自約敕諸父曰：「汝等後世若富貴於今日者，慎勿積金一斤、彩帛百匹已上，用為富也。 」不聽興生求利，又不聽與勢家作婚姻。 至吾兄弟，不能遵奉。 今汝等服乘漸華好，吾是以知恭儉之德，漸不如上也。 又吾兄弟，若在家，必同盤而食； 若有近行，不至，必待其還。 亦有過中不食，忍饑相待。 吾兄弟八人，今存者有三，是故不忍別食也。 又願畢吾兄弟，不異居異財。 汝等眼見，非為虛假。 如聞汝等兄弟，時有別齋獨食者。 此又不如吾等一世也。 吾今日不為貧賤，然居住舍宅，不作壯麗華飾者，正慮汝等後世不賢，不能保守之，將為勢家所奪。
From the day our house entered Wei we have been honored guests of the throne. From then until now, governors of two-thousand-bushel rank have never ceased in our line, and salaries and stipends have been abundant. At weddings and funerals among kin, in-laws, and old friends we have always given lavish gifts; guests who come and go have always been feasted with wine and meat, so that kin and friends have had no cause for complaint. In the founding days of the state, men liked to dress in bright colors. I do not recall affairs in the time of the Shanggu elder, but I remember how the Qinghe elder dressed. I always saw him in plain cloth and a leather belt. He often admonished his brothers: "If you later grow richer than we are today, take care not to amass more than one jin of gold or a hundred bolts of colored silk." " He forbade trade for profit and forbade marriage alliances with powerful families. We brothers could not live up to his example. Your dress and mounts grow ever more splendid; I see that respect and frugality are fading with each generation. When we brothers were at home we always ate from the same dish; if one was away on a short errand, we waited until he returned. Sometimes we passed midday without eating, enduring hunger while we waited. We were eight brothers; only three survive today—that is why we could not bear to eat apart. I also charge you: for the rest of our days, do not live apart or hold separate estates. You have seen this yourselves—it is no empty lesson. I hear that some of you brothers now take separate rooms and eat alone. This too falls short of our generation. I am not poor today, yet I do not build a splendid house, precisely because I fear that if you prove unworthy in later generations you will not keep it and powerful families will seize it.

北都時，朝法嚴急。 太和初，吾兄弟三人並居內職：兄在高祖左右，吾與津在文明太后左右。 于時口敕，責諸內官，十日仰密得一事，不列便大嗔嫌。 諸人多有依敕密列者，亦有太后、高祖中間傳言構間者。 吾兄弟自相誡曰：「今忝二聖近臣，居母之間難，宜深慎之。 又列人事，亦何容易，縱被嗔責，勿輕言。 」十餘年中，不嚐言一人罪過。 時大被嫌責，答曰：「臣等非不聞人語，正恐不審，仰誤聖聽，以是不敢言。 」於後終以不言。 蒙賞及二聖間言語，終不敢輒爾傳通。 太和二十一年，吾從濟州來朝，在清徽堂豫宴。 高祖謂諸貴曰：「北京之日，太后嚴明，吾每得杖。 左右因此有是非言。 和朕母子者，唯楊播兄弟。 」遂舉爵賜兄及我酒。 汝等脫若萬一蒙明主知遇，宜深慎言語，不可輕論人惡也。 吾自惟文武才藝、門望姻援不勝他人。 一旦位登侍中、尚書，四曆九卿，十為刺史，光祿大夫、儀同、開府、司徒、太保，津今復為司空者，正由忠謹慎口，不嚐論人之過，無貴無賤，待之以禮，以是故至此耳。 聞汝等學時俗人，乃有坐待客者，有驅馳勢門者，有輕論人惡者； 及見貴勝則敬重之，見貧賤則慢易之，此人行之大失，立身之大病也。 汝家仕皇魏以來，高祖以下乃有七郡太守、三十二州刺史，內外顯職，時流少比。 汝等若能存禮節，不為奢淫驕慢，假不勝人，足免尤誚，足成名家。 吾今年始七十五，自惟氣力，尚堪朝覲天子，所以孜孜求退者，正欲使汝等知天下滿足之議，為一門法耳，非是苟求千載之名。 汝等能記吾言，吾百年後終無恨矣。
In the days of the northern capital, court law was harsh and exacting. Early in the Taihe era we three brothers all held posts within the palace: my elder brother at Emperor Gaozu's side, Jin and I at Empress Dowager Wenming's side. By oral edict the inner officials were charged: within ten days each must secretly obtain one reportable matter; failure brought fierce reprimand. Many obeyed and filed secret reports; others passed words between the empress dowager and the emperor to sow discord. We admonished one another: "We serve as close ministers to the Two Sages; to stand between mother and son is perilous and demands the deepest caution." Reporting on others is no light matter; even if we are scolded, we must not speak rashly." " For more than ten years we never once denounced a single person's fault. When we were sharply rebuked we answered, "We are not deaf to men's talk; we only fear we may judge wrongly and mislead Your Sagely Hearing—that is why we dare not speak." " In the end we were left in peace because we would not speak. Though we were rewarded, we never dared lightly to relay what passed between the Two Sages. In the twenty-first year of Taihe I came to court from Jizhou and attended a banquet in the Qinghui Hall. Emperor Gaozu told the assembled nobles, "In the days at the northern capital the empress dowager was strict and clear-sighted; I was often beaten with the staff." Those at my side therefore spread gossip between them. Only the brothers Yang Bo kept peace between my mother and me. " He raised his goblet and bestowed wine on my elder brother and me. If by any chance you win an enlightened lord's favor, be deeply cautious in speech and never lightly discuss another man's faults. I myself know that in civil and military talent, family standing, and marital connections I do not surpass others. Jin has risen to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of the Masters of Writing, served four times among the Nine Ministers, held ten regional inspectorates, and filled posts from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Yitong through Commissioner with Full Staff, Minister over the Masses, and Grand Guardian — and he is Minister of Works again today — solely because he is loyal, careful, and guarded in speech, never discusses others' faults, and treats everyone, high or low, with courtesy. That is how he came so far. I hear that in your studies you imitate vulgar men: some sit idly waiting for callers, some rush to the gates of the powerful, and some speak lightly of others' faults; When they meet the powerful they show respect, and when they meet the poor they treat them with contempt — that is a grave moral failure and a fatal flaw in how a man conducts his life. Since your family entered imperial service under the Wei, from the time of the High Ancestor down there have been seven commandery administrators and thirty-two regional inspectors, with distinguished posts at court and in the provinces — few families of the age can match that record. If you can hold to proper conduct and avoid extravagance, dissipation, arrogance, and insolence, then even if you never surpass others you will still escape reproach and preserve the family's good name. I am only seventy-five this year, and by my strength I could still attend court and pay homage to the emperor. I press so hard for retirement because I want you to learn the virtue of knowing when enough is enough and make that the rule of our house — not because I crave a name that will last a thousand years. If you remember what I have said, I shall have no regrets after I am gone.

Chun went back to Huayin. More than a year later he was killed by Erzhu Tianguang, and everyone at the time mourned and resented his death. At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief, and Regional Inspector of Ji Province. He had a son named Yu.

Yu, whose courtesy name was Yuanlue, began his career as Left Regular Attendant to Prince Huai of Guangping. Prince Huai loved military affairs and often went hunting, and Yu repeatedly remonstrated with him. During the Zhengshi era, because the retainers of the Jingzhao and Guangping princely establishments had grown lawless, the court ordered Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang to investigate. More than thirty men were executed in the capital market, the rest were dismissed from office, and only Yu and Cui Kai of Boling were spared because their loyal remonstrance had been noted. He was later appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.

初，尚書令王肅除揚州刺史，出頓洛陽東亭。 酣後，廣陽王嘉、北海王詳等與播論議競理，播不為屈。 北海王顧昱曰：「尊伯性剛不伏理，大不如尊使君也。 」昱對曰：「昱父道隆則從其隆，道洿則從其洿； 伯父剛則不吐，柔亦不茹。 」坐歎其能言。 肅曰：「非此郎，何得申二父之美。」
Once, when Wang Su, Minister of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Regional Inspector of Yang Province, he paused on his way out at the Eastern Pavilion of Luoyang. After the wine had gone around, Prince Jia of Guangyang, Prince Xiang of Beihai, and others argued doctrine with Yang Bo, but Bo would not be beaten. The Prince of Beihai turned to Yu and said, "Your uncle's temper is so unyielding that he will not bow to reason — nothing like your father when he was regional inspector." Yu replied, "When my father's way is lofty, I follow its loftiness; when it is low, I follow its lowness;" "my uncle, if the matter is hard he will not spit it out, and if it is soft he will not swallow it either." Those seated there all sighed in admiration at how well he spoke. Su said, "Without this young man, how could the virtues of the two fathers ever have been brought out?"

延昌三年，以本官帶詹事丞。 時明帝在懷抱中，至於出入，左右、乳母而已，不令宮寮聞知。 昱諫曰：「陛下不以臣等凡淺，備位宮臣，太子動止，宜令翼從。 自比以來，輕爾出入，進無二傅導引之美，退闕群寮陪侍之式。 非所謂示人軌儀，著君臣之義。 陛下若召太子，必降手敕，令臣下咸知，為後世法。 」於是詔自今若非手敕，勿令兒輒出，宮臣在直者，從至萬歲門。 轉太尉掾，兼中書舍人。
In the third year of the Yan-chang era he retained his original post while also serving as Assistant to the Household Mentor. At that time Emperor Ming was still an infant in arms, and when he went in and out of the palace only his attendants and wet nurses accompanied him; the palace staff were kept from knowing. Yu remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty, not considering us unworthy, has appointed us as palace officials, so the crown prince's comings and goings ought to be attended by us." Since then he has come and gone too casually: when he goes out he lacks the proper guidance of the two tutors, and when he returns he lacks the formal attendance of the assembled officials. This is not the way to display proper conduct to the world or to make the relation between ruler and minister clear. If Your Majesty summons the crown prince, you should issue a handwritten edict so that all officials know of it and so that later ages may have a precedent. An edict was then issued: from that time forward the child was not to leave the palace unless there was a handwritten order, and the palace officials on duty were to accompany him as far as the Gate of Ten Thousand Years. He was transferred to a clerkship in the Ministry of War and concurrently served as Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.

靈太后嘗謂昱曰：「親姻在外，不稱人心，卿有所聞，慎勿諱隱。 」昱奏揚州刺史李崇五車載貨，恆州刺史楊鈞造銀食器十具，並餉領軍元叉。 靈太后令召叉夫妻，泣而責之。 叉深恨昱。 昱第六叔舒妻，武昌王和之妹，和即叉之從祖父。 舒早喪，有一男六女，及終喪，元氏請別居。 昱父椿集親姻泣謂曰：「我弟不幸早終，今男未婚，女未嫁，何便求別居？ 」不聽。 遂懷憾。 神龜二年，瀛州人劉宣明謀反，事覺逃竄。 叉使和及元氏誣告昱藏宣明，雲昱父椿、叔津並送甲仗三百具，謀圖不逞。 叉又構成其事。 乃遣夜圍昱宅收之，並無所獲。 太后問狀。 昱具對元氏構釁之端，言至哀切。 太后乃解昱縛，和及元氏並處死刑。 而叉相左右，和直免官，元氏卒亦不坐。 及叉之廢太后也，乃出昱為濟陰內史。 中山王熙起兵於鄴，叉遣黃門盧同詣鄴刑熙，並窮黨與。 同希叉旨，就郡鎖昱赴鄴，囚訊百日乃還任。
Empress Dowager Ling once told Yu, "Some of our relatives by marriage in the provinces are unpopular. If you hear anything, do not hide it from me." Yu reported that Li Chong, Regional Inspector of Yang Province, had sent five cartloads of goods, and Yang Jun, Regional Inspector of Heng Province, had made ten sets of silver tableware, both as gifts to the Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha. Empress Dowager Ling had Yuan Cha and his wife summoned and rebuked them through her tears. Cha came to hate Yu deeply. The wife of Yu's sixth uncle Shu was the sister of Prince He of Wuchang, who was Cha's grand-uncle. Shu had died young, leaving one son and six daughters, and when the mourning period ended the Yuan clanswoman asked to set up a separate household. Yu's father Chun gathered the relatives and said through his tears, "My brother died too young. The boy is still unmarried and the girls are still unbetrothed — how can you ask to live apart so soon?" He refused. They therefore nursed a grudge. In the second year of the Sheng-gui era, Liu Xuanming of Ying Province plotted rebellion, and when the plot was discovered he fled. Cha had Prince He and the Yuan clanswoman falsely accuse Yu of harboring Xuanming, claiming that Yu's father Chun and his uncle Jin had each sent three hundred sets of arms and armor in support of a failed plot. Cha then built the case further. Men were sent by night to surround Yu's house and arrest him, but nothing incriminating was found. The empress dowager questioned him about the case. Yu gave a full account of how the Yuan clanswoman had provoked the quarrel, speaking with deep sorrow and urgency. The empress dowager then had Yu unbound, and both Prince He and the Yuan clanswoman were sentenced to death. But because Cha stood at the empress dowager's side, He was merely dismissed from office and the Yuan clanswoman was never punished in the end. When Cha deposed the empress dowager, Yu was sent out to serve as Internal Administrator of Jiyin. When Prince Xi of Zhongshan raised troops at Ye, Cha sent the Yellow Gate official Lu Tong to Ye to execute Xi and root out his associates. Eager to please Cha, Tong went to the commandery, put Yu in chains, and took him to Ye, where he was imprisoned and interrogated for a hundred days before being sent back to his post.

孝昌初，除中書侍郎，遷給事黃門侍郎。 後賊圍豳州，詔昱兼侍中，持節催西北道大都督、北海王顥，仍隨軍監察。 豳州圍解。 雍州蜀賊張映龍、姜神達知州內虛，謀欲攻掩。 刺史元修義懼而請援，一日一夜，書移九通。 都督李叔仁遲疑不赴。 昱曰：「若長安不守，大軍自然瓦散，此軍雖往，有何益也。 」遂與叔仁等俱進，於陣斬神達，諸賊迸散。 詔以昱受旨催督，而顥軍稽緩，遂免昱官。 尋除涇州刺史。 未幾，昱父椿為雍州，征昱除吏部郎中。 及蕭寶夤等敗於關中，以昱兼七兵尚書、持節、假撫軍、都督，防守雍州。 昱遇賊失利而返。 後除鎮東將軍、假車騎將軍、東南道都督，又加散騎常侍。 於後太山守羊侃據郡南叛，侃兄深時為徐州行台，府州咸欲禁深。 昱曰：「昔叔向不以鮒也見廢，奈何以侃罪深，宜呼朝旨。 」不許群議。
At the opening of the Xiao-chang era he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and then promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate. Later, when rebels besieged Bin Prefecture, Yu was made concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary and sent with imperial credentials to hurry Prince Hao of Beihai, Great Commander of the Northwest Route, while accompanying the army as inspector. The siege of Bin Prefecture was lifted. The Shu rebels Zhang Yinglong and Jiang Shenda in Yong Province, seeing that the province was undefended, planned a surprise attack. Regional Inspector Yuan Xiuyi, alarmed, called for help and sent nine dispatches in a single day and night. Commander Li Shuren hesitated and would not march. Yu said, "If Chang'an falls, the main army will collapse of its own accord. Even if we march, what good will it do?" He then advanced with Shuren and the others, killed Shenda in battle, and the rebels broke and fled. An edict blamed Yu for having received orders to hurry the campaign while Hao's army moved too slowly, and Yu was dismissed from office. He was soon appointed Regional Inspector of Jing Province. Before long, when Yu's father Chun became governor of Yong Province, Yu was recalled and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel. After Xiao Baoyin and the others were defeated in Guanzhong, Yu was made concurrent Minister of the Seven Arms, given imperial credentials, named acting General Who Pacifies the Army, and put in command of the defense of Yong Province. Yu met the rebels, was defeated, and withdrew. He was later appointed General Who Pacifies the East, acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander of the Southeast Route, and was also given the post of Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat. Later Yang Kan, Administrator of Taishan, rebelled while holding the commandery in the south. His elder brother Shen was then at the Xuzhou field headquarters, and officials in the prefecture and province all wanted to detain him. Yu said, "In antiquity Shu Xiang was not dismissed because of his son Fuyu. How can we punish Shen for Kan's crime? We should wait for the court's decision." He would not allow the proposal to stand.

還朝未幾，元顥侵逼大梁，除昱南道大都督，鎮滎陽。 顥禽濟陰王暉業，乘虛徑進，城陷。 昱與弟息五人在門樓上。 顥至，執昱下，責曰：「卿今死甘心不？ 」答曰：「分不望生，向所以不下樓，正慮亂兵耳。 但恨八十老父無人供養，乞小弟一命，便是死不朽也。 」顥將陳慶之、胡光等伏顥帳前曰：「陛下度江三千里，無遺鏃費。 昨日殺傷五百餘人，求乞楊昱以快意。 」景曰：「我在江東聞梁主言，初下都，袁昂為吳郡不降，稱其忠節。 奈何殺昱。 」於是斬昱下統帥三十七人，皆令蜀兵刳腹取心食之。
Soon after he returned to court, Yuan Hao pressed toward Daliang, and Yu was made Great Commander of the Southern Route and stationed at Xingyang. Hao captured Prince Ye of Jiyin, exploited the opening to advance straight on the city, and Xingyang fell. Yu was on the gate tower with five younger brothers and sons. When Hao arrived, he had Yu seized and brought down from the tower and demanded, "Are you willing to die now?" He answered, "I never expected to live. I stayed on the tower only because I feared what the disorderly soldiers might do." I only regret that my eighty-year-old father will have no one to care for him. Spare my youngest brother's life, and my death will not have been in vain. Hao's generals Chen Qingzhi, Hu Guang, and others prostrated themselves before his tent and said, "Your Majesty crossed the Yangzi three thousand li without wasting a single arrow." Yesterday more than five hundred men were killed and wounded. We ask that Yang Yu be given to us so that we may have our satisfaction. Jing said, "When I was in the southeast I heard the Liang emperor say that when he first entered the capital, Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wu Commandery, refused to surrender, and he praised his loyalty." How then can we kill Yu? The thirty-seven commanders under Yu were then beheaded, and Shu soldiers were ordered to cut open their bellies, take out their hearts, and eat them.

孝莊還，復前官。 爾硃榮之死，昱為東道行台拒爾硃仲遠。 會爾硃兆入洛，昱還京師。 後歸鄉里，亦為天光所害。 太昌初，贈司空公、定州刺史。
When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to power, Yu was restored to his former offices. After Erzhu Rong's death, Yu served on the Eastern Route field staff to hold off Erzhu Zhongyuan. When Erzhu Zhao took Luoyang, Yu went back to the capital. Later, after he returned home, he too was killed by Erzhu Tianguang. At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as Duke of the Ministry of Works and Regional Inspector of Ding Province.

子孝邕，員外郎，奔免。 匿蠻中，潛結渠率，謀報爾硃氏。 微服入洛，為爾硃世隆所殺。 椿弟穎，字惠哲，本州別駕。
His son Xiaoyong, a Supernumerary Gentleman, fled and escaped capture. He hid among the tribal peoples, secretly rallied local chiefs, and plotted revenge against the Erzhu family. He entered Luoyang in disguise and was killed by Erzhu Shilong. Chun's younger brother Ying, whose courtesy name was Huizhe, served as Vice Administrator of the province.

穎弟順，字延和，寬裕謹厚。 豫立莊帝功，封三門縣伯，位冀州刺史。 罷州還，遇害。 太昌初，贈太尉公、錄尚書事、相州刺史。 子辯，字僧達，位東雍州刺史。
Ying's younger brother Shun, whose courtesy name was Yanhe, was generous, prudent, and solid in character. For helping to establish Emperor Zhuang, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Sanmen County and rose to Regional Inspector of Ji Province. After he left his post and returned home, he was killed. At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as Duke of the Ministry of War, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Regional Inspector of Xiang Province. His son Bian, whose courtesy name was Sengda, served as Regional Inspector of Eastern Yong Province.

辯弟仲宣，有風度才學。 位正平太守，爵恆農伯，在郡有能名。 還京，兄弟與父同遇害。 太昌初，辯贈儀同三司、恆州刺史； 仲宣贈尚書右僕射、青州刺史。
Bian's younger brother Zhongxuan had fine bearing, talent, and learning. He served as Administrator of Zhengping, was ennobled as Baron of Hengnong, and earned a reputation for competence in the commandery. After they returned to the capital, the brothers were killed together with their father. At the opening of the Taichang era Bian was posthumously honored with Yitong rank equal to the Three Excellencies and as Regional Inspector of Heng Province; Zhongxuan was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Regional Inspector of Qing Province.

仲宣子玄就，幼而俊拔。 收捕時，年九歲，牽挽兵人曰：「欲害諸尊，乞先就死。 」兵以刀斫斷其臂，猶請死不止，遂先殺之。 永熙初，贈汝陰太守。
Zhongxuan's son Xuanjiu was precocious and exceptionally gifted. When the arrests were made he was nine years old. Pulling at the soldiers he said, "If you mean to harm my elders, let me die first." A soldier hacked off his arm with a blade, but he still kept begging to die, so they killed him first. At the opening of the Yongxi era he was posthumously honored as Administrator of Ruyin.

順弟津。 津字羅漢，本字延祚，孝文賜改焉。 少端謹，以器度見稱。 年十一，除侍御中散。 時孝文幼沖，文明太后臨朝，津曾入侍左右，忽咳逆失聲，遂吐血數升，藏之衣袖。 太后聞聲，閱而不見，問其故，具以實言，遂以敬慎見知。 賜縑百匹，遷符璽郎中。 津以身在禁密，不外交遊，至宗族姻表罕相參侯。 司徒馮誕與津少結交友，而津見其貴寵，每恆退避，及相招命，多辭疾不往。 誕以為恨，而津逾遠焉。 人或謂之曰：「司徒，君之少舊，何自外也？ 」津曰：「為勢家所厚，復何容易！ 但全吾今日，亦足矣。 」轉振威將軍，領監曹奏事令。 孝文南征，以津為都督、征南府長史。 後遷長水校尉，仍直閣。
Shun's younger brother was Jin. Jin, whose courtesy name was Luohan, had originally been styled Yanzuo; Emperor Xiaowen granted him the new name. From youth he was upright and careful, and won praise for his bearing and capacity. At eleven he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace Guard. Emperor Xiaowen was still a child and Empress Dowager Wenming held court. Once while attending at the emperor's side, Jin suddenly suffered a violent coughing fit, lost his voice, and spat up several sheng of blood, which he concealed in his sleeve. The empress dowager heard the sound, looked but saw nothing, and asked what had happened. He told her the whole truth, and from that time he was recognized for reverence and prudence. He received one hundred bolts of silk as a reward and was promoted to Gentleman of the Seals and Tallies. Because Jin served in the palace's inner confidential ranks, he did not socialize outside court, and even with clan and affinal kin he rarely paid calls. Minister over the Masses Feng Dan had been Jin's friend since youth, but Jin, seeing how favored and powerful he had become, constantly kept his distance; when Feng summoned him, he often pleaded illness and stayed away. Dan resented this, and Jin kept himself ever more aloof. Someone said to him, "The Minister over the Masses is an old friend of yours — why keep him at arm's length?" Jin replied, "When a powerful house favors you, nothing comes easily!" Simply to preserve myself as I am today is enough. He was transferred to General Who Quells Might and concurrently appointed Director of Memorials in the Supervisory Bureau. When Emperor Xiaowen marched south on campaign, Jin was appointed area commander and chief clerk of the southern expedition headquarters. He was later transferred to Colonel of the Long River while continuing to serve in the Direct Attendance.

景明中，宣武游於北芒，津時陪從。 太尉、咸陽王禧謀反，帝馳入華林。 時直閣中有同禧謀，皆在從限。 及禧平，帝顧謂朝臣曰：「直閣半為逆黨，非至忠者安能不豫此謀。 」因拜津左中郎將，遷驍騎將軍，仍直閣。
During the Jingming era Emperor Xuanwu toured Beimang, and Jin accompanied him. Grand Commandant and Prince of Xianyang, Xi, plotted rebellion, and the emperor galloped into Hualin Park. At that time some members of the Direct Attendance had joined Xi's plot, and all were within the imperial entourage. After Xi was suppressed, the emperor turned to the court ministers and said, "Half the Direct Attendance were rebels — only the most loyal could have stayed clear of this plot." He then appointed Jin Left Commandant of the Palace Guard, promoted him to General of Valiant Cavalry, and kept him in the Direct Attendance.

出除岐州刺史，津巨細躬親，孜孜不倦。 有武功人齎絹三匹，去城十里，為賊所劫。 時有使者馳驛而至，被劫人因以告之。 使者到州，以狀白津。 津乃下教，雲有人著某色衣，乘某色馬，在城東十里被殺，不知姓名。 若有家人，可速收視。 有一老母行哭而出，雲是己子。 於是遣騎追收，並絹俱獲。 自是闔境畏服。 至於守令寮佐有濁貨者，未曾公言其罪，常以私書切責之。 於是官屬感厲，莫有犯法者。 以母憂去職。
He was sent out as Regional Inspector of Qi Province and personally attended to every detail without slackening. A man from Wugong was carrying three bolts of silk when, ten li from the city, he was robbed by bandits. A courier happened to arrive by post relay, and the robbed man told him what had happened. When the courier reached the province he reported the matter to Jin. Jin then issued an order stating that someone wearing a certain-colored garment and riding a certain-colored horse had been killed ten li east of the city, identity unknown. If any family member recognized him, they should come at once to claim the body. An old woman came out weeping, saying the victim was her son. He then sent horsemen in pursuit, and both the robbers and the silk were recovered. From then on the whole jurisdiction feared and submitted to his authority. When prefects, magistrates, or staff assistants had taken corrupt gains, he never publicly denounced them but always rebuked them sharply in private letters. The officials were moved by this, and none dared break the law. He left office to mourn his mother.

延昌末，起為華州刺史，與兄播前後牧本州，當世榮之。 先是，受調絹度尺特長，在事因緣，共相進退，百姓苦之。 津乃令依公尺度其輸物，尤好者賜以杯酒而出； 其所輸少劣者，為受之，但無酒以示其恥。 於是競相勸厲，官調更勝。
At the end of the Yanchang era he was recalled as Regional Inspector of Hua Province. He and his elder brother Bo had successively governed their native province, and their contemporaries regarded this as a great honor. Previously, officials collecting tax silk had used extra-long measuring rods, colluding with one another to squeeze the people, who suffered greatly. Jin ordered that all deliveries be measured by the standard public rod. Those of especially fine quality he rewarded with a cup of wine before sending them on their way; those who delivered inferior goods he still accepted, but gave no wine, shaming them by the omission. People then competed to improve their deliveries, and the official levy rose sharply.

孝昌中，北鎮擾亂，侵逼舊京，乃加津安北將軍，北道大都督，尋轉左衛，加撫軍將軍。 津始受命，出據靈丘。 而賊帥鮮于修禮起於博陵，定州危急，遂回師南赴。 始至城下，榮壘未立，而州軍新敗。 津以賊既乘勝，士眾榮疲，柵壘未安，不可擬敵，欲移軍入城，更圖後舉。 刺史元固稱賊既逼城，不可示弱，乃閉門不內。 津揮刃欲斬門者，軍乃得入。 賊果夜至，見柵空而去。 其後，賊攻州城東面，已入羅城。 刺史閉小城東門，城中騷擾。 津開門出戰，賊退，人心少安。 尋除定州刺史，又兼吏部尚書、北道行台。 初，津兄椿得罪此州，由钜鹿人趙略投書所致。 及津至，略舉家逃走。 津乃下教慰喻，令其還業。 於是闔州愧服，遠近稱之。 時賊帥鮮于修禮、杜洛周賤掠州境，孤城獨立，在兩寇之間。 津修理戰具，更營雉堞。 又於城中去城十步，掘地至泉，廣作地道，潛兵湧出，置爐鑄鐵，持以灌賊。 賊遂相告曰：「不畏利槊堅城，唯畏楊公鐵星。 」津與賊帥元洪業等書喻之，並授鐵券，許之爵位，令圖賊帥毛普賢。 洪業等感寤，復書雲欲殺普賢。 又云：「賊欲圍城，正為取北人，城中所有人，必須盡殺。 」津以城內北人，雖是惡黨，然掌握中物，未忍便殺，但收內子城，防禁而已。 將吏無不感其仁恕。 朝廷初送鐵券二十枚，委津分給。 津隨賊中首領，間行送之； 修禮、普賢頗亦由此而死。
During the Xiaochang era the northern garrisons fell into turmoil and threatened the old capital. Jin was given the additional titles of General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Area Commander of the Northern Route, then transferred to the Left Guard with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Army. When Jin first received his commission he marched out and took position at Lingqiu. But the rebel leader Xianyu Xiuli rose at Boling, Ding Province was in grave peril, and Jin turned his army south to its relief. When he first reached the city, his camp fortifications were not yet in place and the provincial army had just suffered defeat. Jin judged that the rebels were riding their victory, his troops were exhausted, and his defenses were not yet secure, so he could not meet the enemy in the field. He wanted to move his army into the city and plan his next move. Regional Inspector Yuan Gu argued that with the rebels already at the walls they must not show weakness, and closed the gates, refusing to admit them. Jin raised his blade as if to strike the gatekeepers, and only then was his army admitted. The rebels came by night, found the camp abandoned, and withdrew. Later the rebels attacked the eastern side of the provincial city and broke into the outer enclosure. The regional inspector closed the inner city's eastern gate, and panic spread through the city. Jin opened the gate and sallied forth; the rebels retreated and the people's spirits steadied somewhat. He was soon appointed Regional Inspector of Ding Province while also serving as Minister of the Masters of Writing and head of the Northern Route Mobile Headquarters. Earlier Jin's elder brother Chun had fallen afoul of this province because Zhao Lue of Julu had submitted a denunciatory letter. When Jin arrived, Lue fled with his entire household. Jin issued a reassuring proclamation and told them to return to their livelihood. The whole province was shamed into submission, and people near and far praised him. At that time the rebel leaders Xianyu Xiuli and Du Luozhou ravaged the province, and the isolated city stood alone between two enemy forces. Jin repaired the war equipment and rebuilt the battlements. He also dug tunnels ten paces inside the wall down to the water table, sent troops out through them in secret, set up furnaces to cast molten iron, and poured it on the rebels. The rebels then told one another, "We do not fear sharp spears or stout walls — we only fear Lord Yang's molten iron." Jin wrote to the rebel leaders Yuan Hongye and others to win them over, granted them iron certificates of mercy, promised them noble ranks, and urged them to turn against the rebel leader Mao Puxian. Hongye and the others were moved by his appeal and wrote back saying they would kill Puxian. They also wrote, "The rebels mean to besiege the city only to seize the northerners within it — every one of them must be killed." Jin could not bring himself to slaughter the northerners in the city, wicked though many of them were, since they still held property there. He only confined them to the inner citadel under guard. The officers and officials were all moved by his humanity and forbearance. The court initially sent twenty iron certificates of mercy and entrusted Jin to distribute them. Jin sent them by secret routes to the rebel leaders; and Xiuli and Puxian were largely killed as a result.
41
既而杜洛周圍州城，津盡力捍守。 詔加衛將軍，將士有功者任津科賞，兵人給復八年。 葛榮以司徒說津。 津大怒，斬其使以絕之。 自受攻圍，經歷三稔，朝廷不能拯赴。 乃遣長子遁突圍出。 詣蠕蠕主阿那瑰，令其討賊。 遁日夜泣訴，阿那瑰遣其從祖吐豆發率精騎南出。 前鋒已達廣昌，賊防塞益口，蠕蠕遂還。 津長史李裔引賊入，津苦戰不敵，遂見拘執。 洛周脫津衣服，置地牢下數日，將烹之。 諸賊還相諫止，遂得免害。 津曾與裔相見，對諸賊帥以大義責之，辭淚俱發，裔大慚。 典守者以告洛周，弗之責。 及葛榮並洛周，復為榮所拘。 榮破，始得還洛。
Soon afterward Du Luozhou besieged the provincial city, and Jin defended it with all his strength. An edict added the rank of General of the Guard, authorized Jin to reward meritorious officers and soldiers as he saw fit, and granted common soldiers eight years' tax exemption. Ge Rong tried to win Jin over with the offer of Minister over the Masses. Jin was furious, beheaded the envoy, and broke off all contact. From the time the siege began three full years passed, and the court could not come to his relief. He then sent his eldest son Dun to break through the encirclement. Dun went to the Rouran ruler Anagui and asked him to attack the rebels. Dun wept and pleaded day and night, and Anagui sent his father's younger cousin Tudufa south at the head of elite cavalry. The vanguard had already reached Guangchang, but the rebels blocked Yikou, and the Rouran withdrew. Jin's chief clerk Li Yi let the rebels in. Jin fought bitterly but could not hold, and was taken captive. Luozhou stripped Jin of his clothes, threw him into a dungeon for several days, and was about to boil him alive. The rebels admonished one another and stopped it, and he escaped with his life. Jin once confronted Yi before the rebel chiefs and rebuked him on grounds of loyalty and duty, his words mingled with tears; Yi was deeply ashamed. The jailer reported this to Luozhou, who did not punish Jin for it. When Ge Rong absorbed Luozhou's forces, Jin was again held captive by Ge Rong. When Ge Rong was defeated, Jin was at last able to return to Luoyang.

永安二年，兼吏部尚書。 元顥內逼，莊帝將親出討，以津為中軍大都督，兼領軍將軍。 未行，顥入。 及顥敗，津乃入宿殿中，掃灑宮掖，遣第二子逸封閉府庫，各令防守。 及帝入也，津迎於北芒，流涕謝罪。 帝深嘉慰之。 尋以津為司空，加侍中。 爾硃榮死，使津以本官為兼尚書令、北道大行台、都督、并州刺史，委以討胡經略。 津馳至鄴，將從滏口而入。 遇爾硃兆等已克洛，相州刺史李神等議欲與津舉城通款，津不從。 以子逸既為光州刺史，兄子昱時為東道行台，鳩率部曲，在於梁、沛，津規欲東轉，更為方略。 乃率輕騎望於濟州度河。 而爾硃仲遠已陷東郡，所圖不果，遂還京師。 普泰元年，亦遇害於洛。 太昌初，贈大將軍，太傅、都督、雍州刺史，諡曰孝穆。 將葬本鄉，詔大鴻臚持節監護喪事。 長子遁。
In the second year of Yong'an he also served as Minister of the Masters of Writing. When Yuan Hao pressed inward, Emperor Zhuang prepared to lead the campaign in person and appointed Jin Grand Area Commander of the Central Army while also making him General of the Palace Guard. Before the emperor could set out, Hao entered the capital. When Hao was defeated, Jin took up residence in the palace, swept and cleaned the inner quarters, sent his second son Yi to seal the treasuries, and posted guards at each. When the emperor returned, Jin met him at Beimang in tears, begging forgiveness. The emperor warmly praised and reassured him. Jin was soon appointed Minister of Works with the additional rank of Palace Attendant. After Erzhu Rong's death, Jin was ordered to retain his present office while also serving as Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, head of the Northern Route Grand Mobile Headquarters, area commander, and Regional Inspector of Bing Province, entrusted with the campaign against the rebels. Jin galloped to Ye and planned to enter through the Fu Pass. He found that Erzhu Zhao and others had already taken Luoyang. Regional Inspector of Xiang Province Li Shen and others proposed surrendering the city to Jin and opening negotiations, but Jin refused. His son Yi was already Regional Inspector of Guang Province, and his elder brother's son Yu then headed the Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters, each gathering troops in Liang and Pei. Jin planned to turn east and devise a new strategy. He then led light cavalry toward Jizhou to cross the river. But Erzhu Zhongyuan had already taken Dong Commandery, his plan failed, and he returned to the capital. In the first year of Putai he was likewise killed at Luoyang. At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as General-in-Chief, Grand Tutor, area commander, and Regional Inspector of Yong Province, with the posthumous name Xiaomu (Filial and Solemn). When he was to be buried in his native district, an edict ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to supervise the funeral with full ceremonial authority. His eldest son was Dun.

遁字山才。 其家貴顯，諸子弱冠，咸縻王爵。 而遁性靜退，年近三十，方為鎮西府主簿。 累遷尚書左丞、金紫光祿大夫，亦被害於洛。 太昌初，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史，諡曰恭定。
Dun, whose style name was Shancai. His family was eminent and powerful, and when the sons came of age they all received princely titles. But Dun was quiet and retiring by nature, and not until he was nearly thirty did he become chief clerk of the Western Garrison Headquarters. He rose in stages to left assistant in the Masters of Writing and grand master of splendid happiness with purple-gold seal, and was also killed at Luoyang. At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as general of the cavalry and chariots, with honors equal to the three excellencies, and inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Gongding (Respectful and Settled).

遁弟逸，字遵道，有當世才。 起家員外散騎侍郎，以功賜爵華陰男。 建義初，莊帝猶在河陽，逸獨往謁。 帝特除給事黃門侍郎，領中書舍人。 及朝士濫禍，帝益憂怖，詔逸晝夜陪侍，常寢御床前。 帝曾夜中謂逸曰：「昨來舉目唯見異人，賴卿差以自慰。 」再遷南秦州刺史，加散騎常侍，時年二十九，時方伯之少，未有先之者。 仍以路阻不行，改光州刺史。 時災儉連歲，逸欲以倉粟振給，而所司懼罪不敢。 逸曰：「國以人為本，人以食為命，假令以此獲戾，吾所甘心。 」遂出粟，然後申表。 右僕射元羅以下，謂公儲難闕，並執不許。 尚書令、臨淮王彧以為宜貸二萬，詔聽貸二萬。 逸既出粟之後，其老小殘疾不能自存活者，又於州門造粥飼之，將死而得濟者以萬數。 帝聞而善之。 逸為政愛人，尤憎豪猾，廣設耳目，善惡畢聞。 其兵出使下邑，皆自持糧，人或為設食者，雖在暗室，終不敢進，咸言楊使君有千里眼，那可欺之。 在州政績尤美。
Dun's younger brother Yi, styled Zundao, had talent to match his times. He entered service as a supernumerary cavaliers-attendant and was ennobled as Baron of Huayin for his achievements. At the opening of the Jianyi era, while Emperor Zhuang was still at Heyang, Yi went alone to pay his respects. The emperor specially appointed him gentlemen-in-attendance of the yellow gate and made him concurrent secretariat gentleman. When court officials were slaughtered indiscriminately, the emperor grew increasingly fearful. An edict ordered Yi to attend day and night, and he regularly slept beside the imperial couch. Once at night the emperor said to Yi, "Yesterday I looked around and saw only strangers; thanks to you I find a little comfort." He was next made inspector of Southern Qin while also appointed regular cavaliers-attendant. At twenty-nine he was the youngest regional governor anyone could remember. Because the roads were blocked he could not take up the post and was reassigned as inspector of Guangzhou. Famine had struck for years running, and Yi wanted to distribute grain from the storehouses, but the responsible officials feared punishment and dared not act. Yi said, "The state is built on people, and people live by food. Even if I should be punished for this, I accept it willingly." He released the grain and only afterward submitted a memorial reporting it. Right Vice Director Yuan Luo and others argued that the public granaries could not be depleted, and all objected. Minister over the Masters of Writing, the Prince of Linhuai Yu, thought twenty thousand should be lent; an edict authorized a loan of twenty thousand. After releasing the grain, he set up gruel kitchens at the provincial gate for the old, young, disabled, and destitute. Tens of thousands who had been at death's door were saved. The emperor heard of it and praised him. In office Yi cared for the people, hated the powerful and dishonest, and maintained a wide network of informants so that he heard of every deed, good or ill. When his soldiers went on missions to subordinate districts they carried their own provisions. Even if someone offered them food in private, they would not dare accept it, saying Intendant Yang had eyes everywhere and could not be fooled. His record in the province was especially distinguished.

及其家禍，爾硃仲遠遣使於州害之。 吏人如喪親戚，城邑村落營齋供，一月之中，所在不絕。 太昌初，贈都督、豫郢二州刺史，諡曰貞。
When disaster struck his family, Erzhu Zhongyuan sent men to the province and had him killed. Officials and commoners mourned him as if he were kin. In towns and villages people set up memorial offerings, and for a full month such observances never ceased. At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as area commander and inspector of Yu and Ying provinces, with the posthumous name Zhen (Upright).

逸弟謐，字遵和。 曆員外散騎常侍，以功賜爵恆農伯，鎮軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫、衛將軍。 在晉陽，為爾硃兆所害。 太昌初，贈驃騎將軍、兗州刺史。 謐弟愔，事列於後。
Yi's younger brother Mi, styled Zunhe. He served as supernumerary regular cavaliers-attendant and was ennobled Baron of Hengnong for merit, rising to general who stabilizes the army, grand master of splendid happiness with purple-gold seal, and general of the guard. While at Jinyang he was killed by Erzhu Zhao. At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as general of agile cavalry and inspector of Yanzhou. Mi's younger brother Yin is treated below.

津弟痈，字延季。 弘厚，頗有文學。 位武衛將軍，加散騎常侍、安南將軍。 莊帝初，遇害河陰，曾儀同三司、雍州刺史。
Jin's younger brother Yong, styled Yanji. He was broad-minded and accomplished in letters. He rose to general of the martial guard, with the added ranks of regular cavaliers-attendant and general who pacifies the south. Early in Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin. He had previously held honors equal to the three excellencies and served as inspector of Yongzhou.

播家世純厚，為並敦議讓，昆季相事，有如父子。 播性剛毅，椿、津恭謙，兄弟旦則聚於査堂，終日相對，未曾入內。 有一美味，不集不食。 査堂間，往往幃慢隔障，為寢息之所，時就休偃，還共談笑。 椿年老，曾他處醉歸，津扶侍還室，仍假寢閣前，承候安否。 椿、津年過六十，並登臺鼎； 而津常旦暮參問，子侄羅列階下，椿不命坐，津不敢坐。 椿每近出，或日斜不至，津不先飯； 椿還，然後共食。 食則津親授匙箸，味皆先嘗，椿命食，然後食。 津為司空，于時府主皆自引寮佐。 人有就津求官者，津曰：「此事須家兄裁之，何為見問。 」初，津為肆州，椿在京宅，每有四時嘉味，輒因使次附之，若或未寄，不先入口。 椿每得所寄，輒對之下泣。 兄弟並皆有孫，唯椿有曾孫，年十五六矣。 椿常欲為之早娶，望見玄孫。 自昱已下，率多學尚，時人莫不欽焉。 一家之內，男女百口，緦服同爨，庭無間言。 魏世以來，唯有盧陽烏兄弟及播昆季，當世莫逮焉。
The Bo family was known for pure-hearted generations, mutual courtesy, and brothers who served one another as faithfully as fathers and sons. Bo was firm by nature, while Chun and Jin were respectful and modest. The brothers spent their days together in the hall, face to face, never withdrawing indoors. They would not taste a fine dish unless all were assembled. Curtains and screens between the halls formed resting places where they would nap and then return to talk and laugh together. When Chun was old, Jin once helped him home after he returned drunk from elsewhere, then slept outside his door to be on hand if needed. Chun and Jin, both past sixty, both reached the highest offices; Yet Jin still attended Chun morning and evening. When nephews filled the steps below, Chun would not tell Jin to sit, and Jin would not dare sit. Whenever Chun went out for the day, if he had not returned by sunset Jin would not eat first; Only when Chun returned would they eat together. At meals Jin personally handed his brother spoon and chopsticks, tasted every dish first, and ate only when Chun told him to. When Jin was Minister of Works, department heads normally introduced their own staff for appointments. When someone came to Jin seeking an office, Jin said, "That is for my elder brother to decide — why ask me?" When Jin was in Si Province and Chun remained in the capital, he always sent seasonal delicacies with the next courier. If they had not yet been sent, he would not taste them first. Whenever Chun received what Jin sent, he wept over it. All the brothers had grandsons, but only Chun had a great-grandson, already fifteen or sixteen. Chun often wished to marry him off early in hopes of seeing a great-great-grandson. From Yu's generation down, most pursued learning, and people of the age admired them. In one household a hundred men and women shared mourning dress and one kitchen, and there was never an angry word in the courtyard. Since the Wei dynasty, only the brothers Lu Yangwu and the Bo brothers had rivaled them — no family of their age could match them.
49
爾硃世隆等將害椿家，誣其為逆，奏請收之。 節閔不許； 世隆復苦執，不得已，乃下詔。 世隆遂遣步騎夜圍其宅，天光亦同日收椿于華陰，東西兩處，無少長皆遇禍，籍沒其家。 節閔惋悵久之。
Erzhu Shilong and others planned to destroy Chun's family, falsely accused them of rebellion, and memorialized requesting their arrest. Emperor Jiemin refused; Shilong pressed again, and the emperor reluctantly issued an edict. Shilong sent foot and horse soldiers by night to surround their residence, and Tianguang on the same day seized Chun at Huayin. In both places, young and old alike perished, and their property was confiscated. Emperor Jiemin grieved over it for a long time.

愔字遵彥，小名秦王。 兒童時，口若不能言； 而風度深敏，出入門閭，未嘗戲弄。 六歲學史書，十一受《詩》、《易》，好《左氏春秋》。 幼喪母，曾詣舅源子恭。 子恭與之飲，問讀何書。 曰：「誦《詩》」。 子恭曰：「誦至《渭陽》未邪？ 」愔便號泣感噎。 子恭亦對之歔欷，遂為之罷酒。 子恭後謂津曰：「常謂秦王不甚察慧，從今已後，更欲刮目視之。」
Yin, styled Zunyan, bore the childhood name Qinwang. As a child he seemed barely able to speak; Yet his bearing was deeply perceptive, and he never frolicked in the streets. At six he studied history; at eleven he began the Book of Songs and the Book of Changes; he loved the Zuo Tradition on the Spring and Autumn Annals. He lost his mother young and once visited his maternal uncle Yuan Zigong. Zigong drank with him and asked what book he was studying. He answered, "Reciting the Book of Songs." Zigong asked, "Have you reached 'Wei Yang' yet?" Yin immediately burst into sobs, choked with grief. Zigong sighed in response and stopped the drinking party. Later Zigong told Jin, "I always thought Qinwang was not very bright. From now on I shall look at him with fresh eyes."
51
愔一門四世同居，家甚隆盛，昆季就學者三十餘人。 學庭前有柰樹，實落地，群兒咸爭之。 愔頹然獨坐。 其季父痈適入學館，見之，大用嗟異。 顧謂賓客曰：「此兒恬裕，有我家風。 」宅內有茂竹，遂為愔于林邊別葺一室，命獨處其中，常銅盤具盛饌以飯之。 因以督厲諸子曰：「汝輩但如遵彥謹慎，自得竹林別室、銅盤重肉之食。 」愔從父兄黃門侍郎昱特相器重，曾謂人曰：「此兒駒齒未落，已是我家龍文； 更十歲後，當求之千里外。 」昱嘗與十餘人賦詩，愔一覽便誦，無所遺失。 及長，能清言，美音制，風神俊悟，容止可觀，人士見之，莫不敬異； 有識者多以遠大許之。
Yin's clan lived together for four generations; the household was prosperous, and more than thirty brothers and cousins attended school together. A nashi tree stood before the school courtyard, and when the fruit fell to the ground all the children scrambled for it. Yin sat apart, unconcerned. His uncle Yong happened into the academy and was deeply impressed. Turning to his guests he said, "This boy is calm and generous — he has our family character." The estate had a grove of bamboo, and Yong had a separate room built for Yin beside it, where he was to live alone. Yong regularly sent him a bronze platter of fine food. He used this to exhort the other boys: "If you are as careful as Zunyan, you too will earn a private room beside the bamboo grove and meals on a bronze platter laden with meat." Yin's elder cousin Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu especially valued him and once said, "This boy still has his milk teeth, yet he is already the dragon of our house." Ten years from now people will seek his like from a thousand leagues away. Yu once composed poems with a dozen others; Yin read them once and recited them without omitting a word. When he grew up he excelled at pure talk, had a fine voice, a sharp and radiant presence, and dignified bearing. Scholars who met him all regarded him with awe; Men of discernment all foretold a great future for him.
52
正光中，隨父之并州。 性既恬默，又好山水，遂入晉陽西縣甕山讀書。 孝昌初，津為定州刺史，愔亦隨父之職。 以軍功除羽林監，賜爵魏昌男，不拜。 及中山為杜洛周陷，全家被囚縶。 未幾，洛周滅，又沒葛榮。 榮欲以女妻之，又逼以偽職。 愔乃托疾，密含牛血數合，於眾中吐之，仍陽喑不語。 榮以為信然，乃止。 永安初，還洛，拜通直散騎侍郎，年十八。
In the Zhengguang era he accompanied his father to Bingzhou. Quiet by nature and fond of landscape, he went to Weng Mountain in Xixian near Jinyang to study. At the opening of the Xiaochang era Jin became inspector of Dingzhou, and Yin accompanied him. For military merit he was appointed supervisor of the feathered forest guard and ennobled Baron of Weichang, but he declined. When Zhongshan fell to Du Luozhou, the entire family was taken captive. Soon after, Luozhou was defeated and they fell into Ge Rong's hands. Rong wished to marry his daughter to Yin and also pressed a bogus office on him. Yin feigned illness, secretly held several he of ox blood in his mouth, vomited it before the crowd, and then played deaf and mute. Rong believed him and dropped the matter. At the opening of the Yongan era he returned to Luoyang and was appointed attendant cavalier for direct counsel at eighteen.

元顥入洛時，愔從父兄侃為北中郎將，鎮河梁。 愔適至侃處，便屬乘輿失守，夜至河。 侃雖奉迎車駕北度，而潛南奔。 愔固諫止之，遂相與扈從達建州。 除通直散騎常侍。 愔以世故未夷，志在潛退，乃謝病。 與友人中直侍郎河間邢邵隱於嵩山。
When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yin's elder cousin Kan was general of the northern gentlemen, stationed at Heliang. Yin happened to reach Kan just as the emperor lost control of the capital and fled by night to the river. Although Kan outwardly escorted the imperial carriage north across the river, he secretly planned to flee south. Yin firmly remonstrated and stopped him, and together they escorted the emperor to Jianzhou. He was appointed regular attendant cavalier for direct counsel. Believing the times were still unsettled, Yin wished to withdraw quietly and pleaded illness. With his friend Attendant-in-Ordinary Xing Shao of Hejian he went into seclusion on Mount Song.
54
及莊帝誅爾硃榮，其從兄侃參贊帷幄。 朝廷以其父津為并州刺史、北道大行台，愔隨之任。 有邯鄲人楊寬者，求義從出籓，愔請津納之。 俄而孝莊幽崩，愔時適欲還都，行達邯鄲，過楊寬家，為寬所執。 至相州，見刺史劉誕，以愔名家盛德，甚相哀念，付長史慕容白澤禁止焉。 遣隊主鞏榮貴防禁送都，至安陽亭，愔謂榮貴曰：「僕百世忠臣，輸誠魏室，家亡國破，一至於此。 雖曰囚虜，復何面目見君父之讎！ 得自縊於一繩，傳首而去，君之惠也。 」榮貴深相矜感，遂與俱逃。 愔乃投高昂兄弟。
When Emperor Zhuang executed Erzhu Rong, his elder cousin Kan served as an adviser in the command tent. The court appointed his father Jin inspector of Bingzhou and head of the Northern Route Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Yin accompanied him to his post. A man of Handan named Yang Kuan asked to follow them out of the province in loyal service, and Yin persuaded Jin to accept him. Soon Emperor Xiaozhuang died in confinement. Yin was then on his way back to the capital; when he reached Handan and passed Yang Kuan's house, Kuan seized him. When he reached Xiangzhou he met Regional Inspector Liu Yan, who pitied Yin as a man of famous lineage and high character and entrusted him to chief clerk Murong Baize for confinement. Team commander Gong Ronggui was sent to guard and escort him to the capital. At Anyang Pavilion Yin said to Ronggui, "My family has served as loyal subjects for generations and gave our hearts to Wei. Now my family is destroyed and the state is broken — and it has come to this." Though I am called a prisoner, how could I face my sovereign's murderers! Let me hang myself, and you carry off my head — that would be a kindness from you. Deeply moved, Ronggui fled with him. Yin then fled to Gao Ang and his brothers.

既潛竄累載，屬齊神武至信都，遂投刺轅門。 便蒙引見，讚揚興運，陳訴家禍，言辭哀壯，涕泗橫集。 神武為之改容，即署行台郎中。 南攻鄴，曆楊寬村，寬于馬前叩頭請罪。 愔謂曰：「人不識恩義，蓋亦常理。 我不恨卿，無假驚怖。 」時鄴未下，神武命愔作祭天文，燎畢而城陷。 由是轉大行台右丞。 于時霸圖草創，軍國務廣，文檄教令皆自愔及崔甗出。
After years in hiding, when Northern Qi founder Gao Huan reached Xindu, Yin presented his calling card at headquarters. Gao Huan received him at once, heard him praise the rising fortune and recount his family's ruin, and was moved by his grief-stricken, impassioned words and streaming tears. Gao Huan's expression softened, and he immediately appointed Yin gentleman of the mobile headquarters. During the southern campaign against Ye they passed through Yang Kuan's village, and Kuan kowtowed before Yin's horse to beg forgiveness. Yin said, "It is only human to fail to recognize gratitude and loyalty." I bear you no grudge, so have no need to fear. Ye had not yet fallen, and Gao Huan ordered Yin to compose an address to Heaven. When the rite was complete the city fell. For this he was made right assistant of the grand mobile headquarters. At that time the new regime was being established and military and civil business was vast; proclamations and edicts issued from Yin and Cui Yan.

遭罹家難，常以喪禮自居，所食唯鹽米而已，哀毀骨立。 神武湣之，常相開慰。 及韓陵之戰，愔每陣先登。 朋僚咸共怪歎曰：「楊氏儒生，今遂為武士，仁者必勇，定非虛論。 」頃之，表請解職還葬，一門之內，贈太師、太傅、丞相、大將軍者二人； 太尉、錄尚書及尚書令者三人； 僕射、尚書者五人； 刺史、太守者二十餘人。 追榮之盛，古今未之有也。 及喪柩進發，吉凶儀衛亙二十餘里，會葬者將萬人。 是日，隆冬盛寒，風雪嚴厚，愔跣步號哭，見者無不哀之。 尋征赴晉陽，仍居本職。
Stricken by family disaster, he lived as if in mourning, eating only salt and rice until grief wore him to skin and bone. Gao Huan pitied him and often comforted him. At the battle of Hanling Yin led every charge. Colleagues marveled and said, "The Yang clan's scholar has become a warrior — the benevolent must be brave; that is no empty saying." Soon afterward he memorialized requesting leave to return for burial. Within the clan alone, two men were posthumously honored as grand preceptor, grand tutor, chancellor, and general-in-chief; grand guardian, supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and minister over the Masters of Writing — three men; vice directors and ministers of the Masters of Writing — five men; regional inspectors and grand administrators — more than twenty men. The scale of posthumous honors was unmatched in history. When the coffin set out, the funeral procession stretched more than twenty li, and nearly ten thousand people attended the burial. That day, in deep winter with fierce wind and snow, Yin walked barefoot weeping. All who saw him were moved to pity. He was soon summoned to Jinyang and resumed his former office.

愔從兄幼卿為岐州刺史，以直言忤旨見誅。 愔聞之悲懼，因哀感發疾，後取急就雁門溫湯療疾。 郭季素害其能，因致書恐之曰：「高王欲送卿於帝所。 」仍勸其逃亡。 愔遂棄衣冠于水濱，若見沈者。 變易名姓，自稱劉士安。 入嵩山，與沙門曇謨征等屏居削跡。 又潛之光州，因東入田橫島，以講誦為業，海隅之士謂之劉先生。 太守王元景陰佑之。
Yin's elder cousin Youqing, regional inspector of Qizhou, was executed for speaking bluntly against the emperor's wishes. When Yin heard this he was stricken with grief and fear, fell ill, and later took emergency leave to treat himself at the hot springs of Yanmen. Guo Jisu, who envied his talent, sent a threatening letter saying, "Lord Gao wishes to send you to the emperor." He also advised him to flee. Yin cast his hat and robes into the river as if he had drowned. He changed his name and surname, calling himself Liu Shi'an. He entered Mount Song and lived in seclusion with the monk Tanmozheng and others, erasing all traces of himself. He secretly went to Guangzhou, then east to Tianheng Island, where he made a living by lecturing and recitation. Coastal scholars called him Master Liu. Grand Administrator Wang Yuanjing secretly sheltered him.
