神武知愔存，遣愔從兄寶猗齎書慰喻； 仍遣光州刺史奚思業令搜訪，以禮發遣。 神武見之悅，除太原公開府司馬，轉長史，復授大行台右丞，封華陰縣侯，遷給事黃門侍郎，妻以庶女。 又兼散騎常侍，為聘梁使主。 至碻磝，州內有愔家舊佛寺。 精廬禮拜，見太傅容像，悲感慟哭，嘔血數升，遂發病不成行，輿疾還鄴。 久之，以本官兼尚書吏部郎中。 武定末，以望實之美，超拜吏部尚書，加侍中、衛將軍，侍學典選如故。
When Gao Huan learned Yin was alive, he sent Yin's elder cousin Baoqi with a letter of reassurance; he also sent Regional Inspector of Guang Province Xi Siye to find him and escort him back with full ceremony. Gao Huan was delighted to see him, appointed him opening staff major to the Duke of Taiyuan, then chief clerk, again made him right assistant of the grand mobile headquarters, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huayin, promoted him to attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate, and married him to a concubine daughter. He also served concurrently as regular cavaliers-attendant and headed an embassy of marriage to Liang. When he reached Que'ao there was an old family Buddhist temple in the province. He worshipped in the temple hall and saw the portrait of the Grand Tutor. Overcome with grief he wailed, vomited blood, fell too ill to travel, and was carried back to Ye. After a long interval he was concurrently made gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in his former rank. Late in the Wuding era, on the strength of his reputation he was promoted over others to minister of the Masters of Writing, with the added ranks of attendant-in-ordinary and general of the guard, while continuing to oversee learning and selection as before.
59
天保初，以本官領太子少傅，別封陽夏縣男。 又詔監太史，遷尚書右僕射。 尚太原長公主，即魏孝靜後也。 會有雉集其舍，又拜開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射，改封華山郡公。 九年，徙尚書令，又拜特進、驃騎大將軍。 十年，封開封王。 文宣之崩，百寮莫有下淚，愔悲不自勝。 濟南嗣業，任遇益隆，朝章國命，一人而已。 推誠體道，時無異議。 乾明元年二月，為孝昭帝所誅，時年五十。 天統末，追贈司空公。
At the opening of the Tianbao era he was appointed junior tutor of the crown prince in his former rank and separately enfeoffed as Baron of Yangxia. An edict also made him supervisor of the grand astrologer, and he was transferred to right vice director of the Masters of Writing. He married the Princess of Taiyuan, who had been Empress of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei. When pheasants gathered at his residence, he was again appointed opening general with honors equal to the three excellencies and right vice director of the Masters of Writing, and his title was changed to Duke of Huashan. In the ninth year he was made minister over the Masters of Writing and again granted special advancement and general of agile cavalry. In his tenth year he was made Prince of Kaifeng. When Emperor Wenxuan died, none of the hundred officials wept; Yin alone was overcome with grief. When Emperor Jinan took the throne, Yang Yin's appointments and favor grew ever greater; court regulations and state policy rested in his hands alone. He gave his heart in sincerity and embodied the Way, and at the time there was no dissent. In the second month of the first year of Qianming he was executed by Emperor Xiaozhao at the age of fifty. Late in the Tiantong era he was posthumously honored as Duke of Works.
60
愔貴公子，早著聲譽，風表鑒裁，為朝野所稱。 家門遇禍，唯有二弟一妹及兄孫女數人。 撫養孤幼，慈旨溫顏，咸出仁厚。 重分義，輕貨財，前後賜與，多散之親族。 群從弟侄十數人，並待而舉火。 頻遭迍厄，冒履艱危，一飡之惠，酬答必重； 性命之仇，舍而不問。 典選二十餘年，獎擢人倫，以為已任。 然取士多以言貌，時致謗言，以為愔之用人，似貧士市瓜，取其大者。 愔聞，不以為意。 其聰記強識，半面不忘。 每有所召，或單稱姓，或單稱名，無有誤者。 後有選人魯漫漢，自言猥賤，獨不見識。 愔曰：「卿前在元子思坊騎禿尾草驢，經見我不下，以方麹鄣面，我何不識卿？ 」漫漢驚服。 又調之曰：「名以定體，漫漢果自不虛。 」又令吏唱人名，誤以盧士深為士琛。 士深自言，愔曰：「盧郎潤朗，所以比玉。」
Yin was a noble scion who won early renown; court and countryside alike praised his bearing and discernment. When disaster struck his family, only two younger brothers, one younger sister, and several of his elder brother's granddaughters survived. He raised the orphaned and young with kindly intent and gentle countenance, all from humane generosity. He valued loyalty and duty over wealth and distributed most of his rewards among his kin. More than ten younger cousins and nephews all relied on him for their livelihood. Repeatedly facing adversity, he braved hardship and danger; he repaid even a single meal's kindness heavily; enemies who threatened his life he spared and did not pursue. For more than twenty years he managed selection, promoting talent and taking it as his own duty. Yet he often chose men by speech and appearance, drawing criticism that Yin's selection was like a poor man buying melons — taking the largest. When Yin heard of it, he paid no attention. His intelligence and memory were formidable; he forgot no face he had seen once. Whenever he summoned someone he might use surname alone or given name alone, and never made a mistake. Later a candidate Lu Manhan said he was lowborn and alone had not been recognized. Yin said, "You once rode a bald-tailed donkey in Yuan Zisi Lane, passed me without dismounting, and covered your face with square-leaven bread — how could I not recognize you?" Manhan was startled and submitted in awe. He also teased him, saying, "The name fixes the substance — Manhan truly lives up to his name." He also had an official call out names and mistakenly called Lu Shishen by the name Shishen. Shishen spoke up for himself; Yin said, "Master Lu is lustrous and bright — that is why he is compared to jade."
61
自尚公主後，衣紫羅袍、金鏤大帶。 遇李庶，頗以為恥，謂曰：「我此衣服，都是內裁，既見子將，不能無愧。」
After marrying the princess he wore purple gauze robes and a great belt inlaid with gold. Meeting Li Shu, he felt somewhat ashamed and said, "These clothes of mine were all cut within the palace; now that I see you, Zijiang, I cannot but feel ashamed."
62
及居端揆，經綜機衡，千端萬緒，神無滯用。 自天保五年已後，一人喪德，維持匡救，實有賴焉。 每天子臨軒，公卿拜授，施號發令，宣揚詔冊，愔辭氣溫辯，神儀秀髮，百寮觀聽，莫不悚動。 自居大位，門絕私交。 輕貨財，重仁義，前後賞賜，積累巨萬，散之九族； 架篋之中，唯有書數千卷。 太保、平原王隆之與愔鄰宅，愔嘗見其門外有富胡數人，謂左右曰：「我門前幸無此物。 」性周密畏慎，恆若不足，每聞後命，愀然變色。
When he occupied the chief minister's seat he managed the pivots of state; amid thousands of threads of business his spirit never stalled. From the fifth year of Tianbao onward, when one man lost virtue, the realm's maintenance and rescue truly depended on him. Whenever the Son of Heaven faced the throne and ministers received appointments, issued orders, and proclaimed edicts, Yin's words were warm and eloquent and his bearing splendid; the hundred officials who watched were all awestruck. Once he occupied the highest position, he shut his gate to private associations. He lightly regarded wealth and heavily valued benevolence and duty; rewards accumulated to vast sums, which he distributed among the nine clans; in his racks and cases there were only several thousand volumes of books. Grand Guardian Prince of Pingyuan Longzhi was Yin's neighbor; Yin once saw several wealthy barbarians outside his gate and said to those beside him, "Fortunately there is nothing like that before my gate." His nature was meticulous and cautious, always as if insufficient; whenever he heard a later appointment his expression changed with alarm.
63
文宣大漸，以常山、長廣二王位地親逼，深以後事為念。 愔與尚書左僕射平秦王歸彥、侍中燕子獻、黃門侍郎鄭子默受遺詔輔政，並以二王威望先重，咸有猜忌之心。 初在晉陽，以大行在殯，天子諒訚，議令常山王在東館，欲奏之事皆先諮決，二旬而止。 仍欲以常山王隨梓宮之鄴，留長廣鎮晉陽。 執政復生疑貳，兩王又俱從至於鄴。 子獻立計。 欲處太皇太后于北宮，政歸皇太后。 又自天保八年已來，爵賞多濫，至是，愔先自表解其開封王，諸叨竊榮恩者皆從黜免。 由是嬖寵失職之徒盡歸心二叔。 高歸彥初雖同德，後尋反動，以疏忌之跡，盡告兩王。 可硃渾天和又每云：「若不誅二王，少主無自安之理。 」宋欽道面奏帝，稱二叔威權既重，宜速去之。 帝不許曰：「可與令公共詳其事。 」愔等議出二王為刺史，以帝仁慈，恐不可所奏，乃通啟皇太后，具述安危。 有宮人李昌儀者，北豫州刺史高仲密之妻，坐仲密事入宮。 太后與昌儀宗情，甚相昵愛。 太后以啟示之，昌儀密白太皇太后。 愔等又議不可令二王俱出，乃奏以長廣王為大司馬、并州刺史，常山王為太師、錄尚書事。 及二王拜職，於尚書省大會百寮，愔等並將同赴。 子默止之云：「事不可量，不可輕脫。 」愔云：「吾等至誠體國，豈有常山拜職，有不赴之理？ 何為忽有此慮？ 」長廣旦伏家僮數十人于錄尚書後室，仍與席上勳貴數人相知，並與諸勳胄約：行酒至愔等，我各勸雙杯，彼必致辭，我一曰「捉酒」，二曰「捉酒」，三曰「何不捉，」爾輩即捉。 及宴如之。 愔大言曰：「諸王反逆，欲殺忠良邪！ 尊天子，削諸侯，赤心奉國，未應及此。 」常山王欲緩之，長廣王曰：「不可。 」於是愔及天和、欽道皆被拳杖亂毆擊，頭面血流，各十人持之。 使薛孤延、康買執子默于尚藥局。 子默曰：「不用智者言，以至於此，豈非命也！」
When Emperor Wenxuan was critically ill, because the princes of Changshan and Changgung were close in rank and position, he was deeply concerned about affairs after his death. Yin, together with left vice director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, attendant-in-ordinary Yan Zixian, and attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate Zheng Zimo, received the deathbed edict to assist in government; because the two princes' prestige had long been weighty, they all harbored suspicions. Initially at Jinyang, because the late emperor's coffin was in mourning and the Son of Heaven was in silent grief, it was proposed that the Prince of Changshan stay in the eastern hall and that all matters to be memorialized should first be consulted and decided — for twenty days only. They still wanted the Prince of Changshan to follow the bier to Ye and the Prince of Changgung to remain and garrison Jinyang. The regents again grew doubtful and divided; both princes followed together to Ye as well. Zixian came up with a plan. They wanted to place the Grand Empress Dowager in the northern palace and return government to the Empress Dowager. Also from the eighth year of Tianbao onward titles and rewards had been lavishly bestowed; at this time Yin first memorialized requesting to relinquish his title as Prince of Kaifeng, and all who had improperly received honors were dismissed. Because of this, favorites who had lost their posts all turned their hearts to the two uncles. Gao Guiyan had at first shared the same purpose, but later turned rebellious and reported all signs of estrangement and suspicion to the two princes. Kezhuhun Tianhe also repeatedly said, "If the two princes are not executed, the young lord has no way to secure himself." Song Qindao memorialized the emperor in person, saying the two uncles' authority and prestige were already great and they should be removed quickly. The emperor refused and said, "This may be discussed in detail with the Chief Minister." Yin and the others proposed sending the two princes out as regional inspectors; because the emperor was benevolent they feared their memorial would not be approved, and so they sent a secret report to the Empress Dowager fully setting forth the danger. There was a palace woman named Li Changyi, wife of Regional Inspector of Northern Yu Gao Zhongmi, who entered the palace because of Zhongmi's case. The Empress Dowager and Changyi were related by clan ties and were very close. The Empress Dowager showed her the secret report, and Changyi secretly informed the Grand Empress Dowager. Yin and the others also argued that the two princes must not both be sent away, and memorialized making the Prince of Changgung grand marshal and inspector of Bingzhou, and the Prince of Changshan grand preceptor and supervisor of the Masters of Writing. When the two princes received their appointments, a great assembly of the hundred officials was held at the Ministry of the Masters of Writing, and Yin and the others were all about to attend together. Zimo stopped them, saying, "The outcome cannot be foreseen — you must not go lightly." Yin said, "We serve the state with utmost sincerity — how could we fail to attend when the Prince of Changshan receives his appointment?" Why these sudden worries? The Prince of Changgung hid several dozen household slaves in the rear chamber behind the supervisor of the Masters of Writing and coordinated with several meritorious nobles at the feast. He agreed with the meritorious scions: when wine reached Yin and the others, each of us will urge a double cup — they will certainly decline — at the first I say 'seize the wine,' at the second 'seize the wine,' at the third 'why not seize?' — then you seize them. At the feast things happened just as he had said. Yin cried out, "Princes, you rebel and plot treason — do you wish to kill the loyal and good!" Honor the Son of Heaven and reduce the feudal lords — with loyal hearts serving the state, this should not come to pass. The Prince of Changshan wanted to ease matters, but the Prince of Changgung said, "It cannot be." Thereupon Yin, Tianhe, and Qindao were beaten with fists and clubs until blood flowed from head and face; ten men each held them. They had Xue Guyian and Kang Mai seize Zimo at the Imperial Medicines Bureau. Zimo said, "Because I did not heed the words of the wise, it has come to this — is this not fate!"
64
二叔率高歸彥、賀拔仁、斛律金擁愔等唐突入雲龍門。 見都督叱利騷，招之不進，使騎殺之。 開府成休寧拒門，歸彥喻之，乃得入。 送愔等於御前。 長廣王及歸彥在硃華門外。 太皇太后臨昭陽殿，太后及帝側立。 常山王以磚叩頭，進而言曰：「臣與陛下骨肉相連。 楊遵彥等欲擅朝權，威福自己，自王公以還，皆重足屏氣，共相脣齒，以成亂階。 若不早圖，必為宗社之害。 臣與湛等為國事重，賀拔仁、斛律金等惜獻皇帝業，共執遵彥等，領入宮，未敢刑戮。 專輒之失，罪合萬死。 」帝時默然。 領軍劉桃枝之徒陛衛，叩刀仰視，帝不睨之。 太皇太后令卻仗不肯，又厲聲曰：「奴輩即今頭落！ 」乃卻。 因問楊郎何在，賀拔仁曰：「一目已出。 」太皇太后愴然曰：「楊郎何所能，留使不好邪？ 」乃讓帝曰：「此等懷逆，欲殺我二兒，次及我耳。 何縱之？ 」帝猶不能言。 太皇太后怒且悲，王公皆泣。 太皇太后曰：「豈可使我母子受漢老嫗斟酌。 」太后拜謝。 常山王叩頭不止。 太皇太后謂帝：「何不安慰爾叔？ 」帝乃曰：「天子亦不敢與叔惜，豈敢惜此漢輩！ 但願乞兒性命，兒自下殿去，此等任叔父處分。 」遂皆斬之。 長廣王以子默昔讒己，作詔書，故先拔其舌，截其手。
The two uncles led Gao Guiyan, Heba Ren, and Hulü Jin in forcing Yin and the others to burst through the Cloud Dragon Gate. They saw Commander Chilì Sao, summoned him but he would not come forward, and had horsemen kill him. Opening General Cheng Xiuning barred the gate; Guiyan persuaded him, and only then could they enter. They brought Yin and the others before the emperor. The Prince of Changgung and Guiyan waited outside the Vermilion Flower Gate. The Grand Empress Dowager came to Zhaoyang Hall; the Empress Dowager and the emperor stood aside. The Prince of Changshan knocked his head on a brick and stepped forward, saying, "Your subject and Your Majesty are joined in flesh and blood. Yang Zunyan and the others wanted to monopolize court power and make authority and favor their own; from the kings and dukes downward all stood on tiptoe holding their breath, mutually supporting one another like lips and teeth, thereby completing the steps of disorder. If we do not act early, they will surely harm the altars of state. Your subject and Zhan and the others, because state affairs were weighty, and Heba Ren, Hulü Jin, and the others cherished the enterprise of Emperor Xianwu, together seized Zunyan and the others and led them into the palace, not yet daring to put them to death. The offense of acting on one's own authority deserves death a thousand times over. The emperor at that moment was silent. The palace guards of Palace Commander Liu Taozhi and the like, with swords drawn, looked up; the emperor would not so much as glance at them. The Grand Empress Dowager ordered them to sheathe their weapons but they refused; she again said fiercely, "Slaves — your heads will fall this instant!" Only then did they fall back. She then asked where Yang Lang was; Heba Ren said, "One of his eyes is already out." The Grand Empress Dowager said sorrowfully, "What harm could Yang Lang do — was it not better to have kept him?" She then reproached the emperor, saying, "These men harbored treason and wished to kill my two sons, and next it would have reached me. Why should they be spared? The emperor still could not find his voice. The Grand Empress Dowager was both angry and grieved; the kings and dukes all wept. The Grand Empress Dowager said, "How could I let my son and me be arranged at the discretion of an old Han woman." The Empress Dowager bowed apologetically. The Prince of Changshan kept knocking his head without cease. The Grand Empress Dowager said to the emperor, "Why will you not comfort your uncle?" The emperor then said, "The Son of Heaven dares not begrudge his uncle — how could he begrudge these Han men!" I only beg for my own life — I will leave the hall myself; these men are yours to dispose of, uncle. Then all were beheaded. The Prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in composing an edict, first pulled out his tongue and cut off his hands.
65
太皇太后臨愔喪，哭曰：「楊郎忠而獲罪。 」以禦金為之一眼，親內之，曰：「以表我意。 」常山亦悔殺之。 先是童謠曰：「白羊頭毣禿，羖腚曆頭生角。 」又曰：「羊羊吃野草，不吃野草遠我道，不遠打爾腦。 」又曰：「阿肼姑，禍也； 道人姑夫，死也。 」羊為愔也，「角」文為用刀，「道人」謂廢帝小名，太原公主嘗作尼，故曰「阿肼姑」，愔、子獻、天和皆尚帝姑，故曰「道人姑夫」云。
The Grand Empress Dowager attended Yin's funeral and wept, saying, "Yang Lang was loyal yet suffered punishment." She made an eye of imperial gold for him, placed it inside, and said, "To express my intent." The Prince of Changshan also came to regret killing him. Earlier there had been a children's song: "White sheep head all bald, ram rump with horn growing on the crown." It also ran, "Sheep sheep eat wild grass; if you do not eat wild grass stay far from my road — if you do not stay far I will smash your head." It also said, "A-bing-gu means calamity;" Dao-ren gu-fu — death. "Sheep" referred to Yin; the character for "horn" contains "use knife"; "Dao-ren" referred to the deposed emperor's childhood name; the Princess of Taiyuan had once become a nun, hence "A-bing-gu"; Yin, Zixian, and Tianhe all married the emperor's aunts, hence "Dao-ren gu-fu."
66
於是乃以天子之命，下詔罪之； 罪止一身，家口不問。 尋復簿錄五家，王晞固諫，乃各沒一房，孩幼盡死，兄弟皆除名。
Then, by the Son of Heaven's command, an edict was issued condemning them; Guilt was limited to the persons themselves; their households were not investigated. Soon afterward the registers of five families were again copied; Wang Xi firmly remonstrated, and so only one branch of each was confiscated; infants and young children were all killed; brothers were all removed from the registers.

遵彥死，仍以中書令趙彥深代總機務。 鴻臚少卿陽休之私謂人曰：「將涉千里，殺騏驥而榮蹇驢，可悲之甚！ 」愔所著詩賦表奏書論甚多，誅後散失，門生鳩集所得者萬餘言。
After Zunyan's death, Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhao Yanshen was again appointed in his stead to oversee the pivots of state. Supervisor of Guests Yang Xiuzhi privately told someone, "About to travel a thousand leagues, yet killing the fine steed and honoring the lame donkey — how lamentable!" Yin wrote a great deal of poetry, fu, memorials, and treatises; after his execution they were scattered and lost, and what his disciples collected amounted to more than ten thousand words.
68
鄭頤字子默，彭城人。 高祖據，魏彭城太守，自滎陽徙焉。 頤聰敏，頗涉文義，而邪險不良。 初為太原公東閣祭酒。 天保世，稍遷中書侍郎。 與宋欽道特相友愛，欽道每師事之。 楊愔始輕宋、鄭，不為之禮。 俄而自結人主，稍不可制。 欽道舊與濟南款狎，共相引致，無所不言。 乾明初，拜散騎常侍，兼中書侍郎。 二人權將楊愔相埒。 愔見害之時，邢子才流涕曰：「楊令君雖其人，死日恨不得一佳伴。 」頤後與愔同詔追贈殿中尚書、廣州刺史。 頤弟抗，字子信，頗有文學。 武平末，兼左右郎中，待詔文林館。
Zheng Yi, styled Zimo, was a man of Pengcheng. His founding ancestor Ju served as Grand Administrator of Pengcheng in Wei and moved from Xingyang. Yi was clever and quick, somewhat versed in letters, but devious and wicked by nature. At first he was libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Duke of Taiyuan. In the Tianbao era he was gradually promoted to attendant gentleman of the secretariat. He was especially friendly with Song Qindao, who always treated him as a teacher. At first Yang Yin looked down on Song and Zheng and did not extend them courtesy. Before long they attached themselves to the ruler and gradually grew beyond control. Qindao had long been intimate with Jinan, drawing one another in; there was nothing they did not discuss. At the beginning of Qianming he was appointed regular cavaliers-attendant and concurrent attendant gentleman of the secretariat. The two men's power nearly matched Yang Yin's. When Yin was killed, Xing Zicai wept and said, "Intendant Yang was indeed the man — on the day of his death he sadly lacked one worthy companion." Later Yi, by the same edict as Yin, was posthumously honored as director of the palace department and inspector of Guangzhou. Yi's younger brother Kang, styled Zixin, was quite accomplished in letters. Late in Wuping he was concurrently left and right gentleman and awaited edicts at the Forest of Literature.
69
楊敷，字文衍，播族孫也。 高祖暉，洛州刺史，贈恆農公，諡曰簡。 曾祖恩，河間太守。 祖鈞，博學強識，頗有幹用。 位七兵尚書、北道行台、恆州刺史、懷朔鎮將，贈侍中、司空公，進封臨貞縣伯，諡曰恭。 父暄，字宣和。 性通朗，強識有學。 位諫議大夫，以別將從廣陽王深征葛榮，遇害。 贈殿中尚書、華州刺史。
Yang Fu, styled Wenyuan, was a clan nephew of Bo. His founding ancestor Hui was regional inspector of Luozhou and was posthumously honored as Duke of Hengnong with the posthumous name Jian (Plain). His great-grandfather En was grand administrator of Hejian. His grandfather Jun was broadly learned with a formidable memory and possessed considerable practical ability. He rose to minister of the seven armies, Northern Route Mobile Headquarters, regional inspector of Hengzhou, and garrison commander of Huaishuo; posthumously he was honored as attendant-in-ordinary and Duke of Works, advanced in enfeoffment to Baron of Linzhen, with the posthumous name Gong (Respectful). His father Xuan, styled Xuanhe. His nature was open and clear, with a formidable memory and learning. He was remonstrance and criticism grandee and as a separate commander followed Prince of Guangyang Shen in campaigning against Ge Rong, and met his end. Posthumously he was honored as director of the palace department and regional inspector of Huazhou.
70
敷少有志操，重然諾，人景慕之。 魏建義初，襲祖鈞爵臨貞縣伯。 稍遷廷尉少卿，斷獄以平允稱。 周孝閔踐阼，進爵為侯。 天和中，為汾州刺史，進爵為公。 齊將段孝先率眾來寇，城陷見禽。 齊人方任用之，敷不為屈，遂以憂憤卒於鄴。 子素。
Fu from youth had resolve and integrity, valued keeping promises, and people admired him. At the opening of the Jianyi era in Wei, he inherited his grandfather Jun's barony of Linzhen. He was gradually promoted to vice director of the Court of Justice and was known for fair and even judgment of cases. When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, his rank was advanced to marquis, the record states. In the Tianhe era he was regional inspector of Fenzhou and his rank was advanced to duke. When Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led troops to invade, the city fell and he was captured, the record states. The Qi were about to employ him, but Fu would not submit; he therefore died of grief and indignation at Ye, the record states. His son was Su.
71
素子處道，少落拓有大志，不拘小節。 世人多未之知，唯從祖寬深異之，每謂子孫曰：「處道逸群絕倫，非常之器，非汝曹所逮。 」後與安定牛弘同志好學，研精不倦，多所通涉。 善屬文，工草隸書，頗留意風角。 美須髯，有英傑之表。
Su's son Chudao from youth was unrestrained with great ambition, not bound by minor rules, the record states. Most people of the age did not know him; only his father's younger cousin Kuan deeply regarded him as extraordinary and often told his sons and grandsons, "Chudao surpasses the crowd and stands alone — an instrument out of the ordinary, not something you can reach." Later he shared the same aspiration with Niu Hong of Anding in loving learning, studying with concentrated effort without weariness, and broadly mastered many fields, the record states. He was skilled at composing prose, adept at cursive and clerical script, and paid considerable attention to wind omens, the record states. He had a fine beard and mustache and the bearing of a heroic champion, the record states.
72
周大塚宰宇文護引為中外記室，轉禮曹，加大都督。 周武帝親總萬機，素以其父守節陷齊，未蒙朝命，上表申理，至於再三。 帝大怒，命左右斬之。 素又言曰：「臣事無道天子，死其分也。 」帝悟其言，贈敷使持節、大將軍、譙、廣、復三州刺史，諡曰忠壯。 拜素車騎大將軍、儀同三司，漸見禮遇。 常令為詔，下筆立成，詞義兼美。 帝嘉之，謂曰：「善相自勉，勿憂不富貴。 」素應聲曰：「臣但恐富貴來逼臣，臣無心圖富貴。」
Grand Regent of Zhou Yuwen Hu invited him as inner and outer recording secretary, transferred him to the Ministry of Rites, and added the rank of grand commander. When Emperor Wu of Zhou personally took charge of all affairs, Su because his father had kept integrity and fallen into Qi without receiving court appointment, memorialized to state his case, reaching to two and three times, the record states. The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered those beside him to behead him, the record states. Su also said, "I serve a ruler without the Way — death is my portion." The emperor took his meaning and posthumously honored Fu with bearer of the staff of authority, general-in-chief, and inspector of Qiao, Guang, and Fu provinces, with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang (Loyal and Stalwart). Su was appointed general of the cavalry and chariots with honors equal to the three excellencies and gradually received courtesy and favor. He was often ordered to draft edicts; he would set brush to paper and finish at once, with both wording and meaning beautiful, the record states. The emperor commended him and said, "Encourage yourself — do not worry about failing to attain wealth and rank." Su answered at once, "I only fear that wealth and rank will press upon me — I have no heart to seek wealth and rank."
73
及隋文帝為丞相，素深自結納，帝甚器之，以為汴州刺史。 至洛陽，會尉遲迥作亂。 滎州刺史宇文胄據武牢應迥，素不得進。 帝拜素大將軍，擊胄破之。 遷徐州總管，位柱國，封清河郡公，以弟岳為臨貞公。 及隋受禪，加上柱國，拜御史大夫。 其妻鄭氏性妒悍，素忿之曰：「我若作天子，卿定不堪為皇后。 」鄭氏奏之，由是坐免。
When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Su deeply attached himself and won favor; the emperor greatly valued him and made him regional inspector of Bianzhou. When he reached Luoyang, Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion, the record states. Regional Inspector of Xingzhou Yuwen Zhou held Wulao in response to Jiong, and Su could not advance. The emperor appointed Su general-in-chief; he attacked Zhou and defeated him. He was transferred to area commander of Xuzhou, attained the rank of pillar of state, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe; his younger brother Yue was made Duke of Linzhen. When Sui received the abdication, he was given the added rank of upper pillar of state and appointed censor-in-chief. His wife Lady Zheng was jealous and fierce; Su said in anger, "If I became Son of Heaven, you certainly could not bear to be empress." Lady Zheng reported this, and because of it he was dismissed from office, the record states.
74
上方圖江表。 先是，素數進取陳計。 未幾，拜信州總管，賜錢百萬、錦千段、馬二百匹遣之。 素居永安，造大艦，名曰五牙，上起樓五層，高百餘尺，左右前後置六檣竿，並高百五十尺，容戰士八百人，旗幟加於上。 次曰黃龍，置兵百餘人。 自余平乘、舴艋等各有差。 及大舉攻伐，以素為行軍元帥，引舟師趣三硤。 至流頭灘，陳將戚欣以青龍百餘艘屯兵守狼尾灘，以遏軍路。 共地險峭，諸將患之。 素曰：「負勝在此一舉，若晝日下船，彼則見我，灘流迅激，制不由人，則吾失其便。 」乃夜掩之。 素親率黃龍十艘，銜枚而下。 遣開府王長襲從南岸擊欣別柵。 令大將軍劉仁恩趣白沙北岸。 比明而至，擊之，欣敗。 虜其眾，勞而遣之，秋毫不犯，陳人大悅。 素率水軍東下，舟艦被江，旌甲曜日。 素坐平乘大船。 容貌雄偉，陳人望之，懼曰：「清河公即江神也。」
The emperor was then planning for the lands south of the Yangzi, the record states. Earlier Su had repeatedly submitted plans for attacking Chen, the record states. Before long he was appointed area commander of Xinzhou and was given a million coins, a thousand bolts of brocade, and two hundred horses and sent off. Su resided at Yong'an and built a great ship called the Five-Tooth, with a tower of five levels rising more than a hundred feet; on left, right, front, and rear were set six mast poles, each a hundred and fifty feet high, holding eight hundred warriors, with banners and flags added above, the record states. Next came the Yellow Dragon, holding more than a hundred soldiers, the record states. The remaining flat-boats, skiffs, and the like each differed in size, the record states. When the great campaign of attack was launched, Su was made field marshal of the campaign and led the fleet toward the Three Gorges. When they reached Liutou Shoals, Chen general Qi Xin with more than a hundred Green Dragon ships stationed troops at Langwei Shoals to block the army's route, the record states. The terrain was steep and narrow; the generals were troubled by it, the record states. Su said, "Victory hangs on this one move. If we disembark by day, they will see us; the shoal currents are swift and violent and cannot be controlled — then we lose our advantage." He therefore attacked by night. Su personally led ten Yellow Dragon ships down with rams in the soldiers' mouths, the record states. He sent Opening General Wang Changxi to strike Xin's separate camp from the south bank, the record states. He ordered Grand General Liu Ren'en to hurry to the north bank of Baisha, the record states. At dawn they arrived and attacked; Xin was defeated. They captured his troops, treated them kindly and sent them away, not violating so much as an autumn hair; the people of Chen were greatly pleased, the record states. Su led the fleet eastward downriver; the ships covered the river, banners and armor dazzling in the sun, the record states. Su sat aboard a flat-decked great ship. He looked heroic and imposing; the people of Chen gazed at him in fear, saying, "The Duke of Qinghe is the river god himself."
75
陳南康內史呂仲肅屯岐亭，正據江峽，於北岸纜岩綴鐵鎖三條，橫截上流，以遏戰船。 素與仁恩登陸俱發，先攻其柵； 仲肅軍夜潰，素徐去其鎖。 仲肅復據荊州之延洲。 素遣巴蜒卒數千，乘五牙四艘，以檣竿碎賊十餘艦，遂大破之，仲肅僅以身免。 陳主遣其信州刺史顧覺鎮安蜀城，荊州刺史陳紀鎮公安，皆懼而走。 巴陵以東，無敢守者。 湘州刺史岳陽王陳叔慎請降。 素下至漢口，與秦孝王會，乃還。 拜荊州總管，進爵郢國公，真食長壽縣千戶； 以其子玄感為儀同三司，玄獎為清河郡公； 賜物萬段，粟萬石，加之金寶； 又賜陳主妹、女妓十四人。 素言於上曰：「裏名勝母，曾子不入，逆人王誼前封郢，臣不願與同。 」於是改封越國公。 尋拜納言，轉內史令。
Chen interior secretary of Nankang Lü Zhongsu garrisoned Qiting, directly holding the river gorge; on the north bank he moored iron chains of three strands across the upper stream to block war ships. Su and Ren'en went ashore together and launched the attack, striking his camp first; Zhongsu's army fled by night; Su slowly removed the chains, the record states. Zhongsu again held Yanzhou of Jing Province, the record states. Su sent several thousand Ba-Yan soldiers in four Five-Tooth ships; with mast poles they smashed more than ten enemy ships, greatly defeated them, and Zhongsu barely escaped with his life, the record states. The Chen ruler sent his regional inspector of Xinzhou Gu Jue to garrison Ancheng and regional inspector of Jingzhou Chen Ji to garrison Gong'an; both were afraid and fled. East of Baling no one dared to hold out. Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou, Prince of Yueyang Chen Shushen requested surrender. Su descended to Hankou and met Prince of Qin Xiaowang, then returned. He was appointed area commander of Jing Province, advanced in rank to Duke of Ying State, with a fief of a thousand households in Changshou County; his son Xuangan was made honors equal to the three excellencies and Xuanjiang Duke of Qinghe; he was given ten thousand lengths of goods, ten thousand shi of grain, with gold and jewels added; he was also given the Chen ruler's younger sister and fourteen female entertainers. Su said to the emperor, "In a district named Shengmu, Zengzi would not enter; the rebel Wang Yi was once enfeoffed as Duke of Ying — I do not wish to share a title with him." Then his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yue State. Soon afterward he was appointed chief counselor and transferred to director of the secretariat.

俄而江南人李稜等為亂，以素為行軍總管討之。 帝命平定日，男子悉斬，女婦賞征人，在陣免者從賤。 賊硃莫問自稱南徐州刺史，以盛兵據京口。 素舟師入自楊子津，進擊破之。 晉陵顧世興自稱太守，與其都督鮑遷等復來拒戰。 素逆擊破之，執遷，虜三千餘人。 進擊無錫賊帥葉皓，又平之。 吳郡沈玄懀、沈傑等以兵圍蘇州，刺史皇甫績頻戰不利，素率眾援之。 玄懀勢迫，走投南沙賊帥陸孟孫。 素擊孟孫于松江，大破之，禽孟孫、玄懀。 黝、歙賊帥沈雪、沈能據柵自固，又攻拔之。
Before long Li Ling and others of the Jiangnan region rebelled, and Su was made field headquarters commander to suppress them. The emperor ordered that on the day of pacification all men were to be beheaded, women given as rewards to the conscript soldiers, and those spared on the battlefield were to be reduced to servile status, the record states. The bandit Zhu Mowen styled himself regional inspector of Southern Xu and with a strong force held Jingkou. Su's fleet entered from Yangzi Ford and advanced to attack and defeat him, the record states. Gu Shixing of Jinling styled himself grand administrator and with his area commander Bao Qian and others again came to resist in battle. Su met and attacked, defeated them, seized Qian, and captured more than three thousand men, the record states. Advancing to attack the Wuxi bandit chief Ye Hao, he pacified him as well, the record states. Shen Xuanyi and Shen Jie of Wu Commandery with troops besieged Suzhou; Regional Inspector Huangfu Ji fought repeatedly without success, and Su led troops to rescue him, the record states. Xuanyi's situation was desperate; he fled to throw himself on the Nansha bandit chief Lu Mengsun, the record states. Su attacked Mengsun at Song River, greatly defeated him, and captured Mengsun and Xuanyi, the record states. The bandit chiefs Shen Xue and Shen Neng of You and She held camps and defended themselves firmly; he again attacked and took them, the record states.
77
江浙賊高智慧自號東揚州刺史，吳州總管五原西元契鎮會稽，以其兵盛而降之。 智慧盡屠其眾，契自殺。 智慧有船艦千餘艘，屯據要害，兵甚勁。 素擊之，自旦至申，苦戰破之。 智慧逃入海。 躡之，從餘姚泛海趣永嘉。 智慧來拒戰，素擊走，賊帥汪文進自稱天子，據東陽，署其徒蔡道人為司空，守樂安。 素進討。 悉平之。 又破永嘉賊帥沈孝徹。 於是步道向天臺，指臨海郡。 遂捕遺逸，前後百餘戰，智慧遁守閩越。 上以素久勞於外，詔令馳傳入朝，加子玄感上開府，賜彩八千段。 素以餘寇未殄，恐為後患，又自請行。 詔以素為元帥，復乘傳至會稽。
The Jiang-Zhe bandit Gao Zhihui styled himself regional inspector of Eastern Yangzhou; area commander of Wu Province Wuyuan Xi Yuanqi garrisoned Kuaiji and submitted to him because his troops were strong. Zhihui slaughtered all his troops to the last man; Yuanqi killed himself, the record states. Zhihui had more than a thousand ships, stationed at strategic points, and his troops were very strong, the record states. Su attacked him; from dawn to the hour of shen he fought bitterly and broke him, the record states. Zhihui fled into the sea, the record states. Su pursued him, going from Yuyao by sea toward Yongjia, the record states. Zhihui came to resist in battle; Su attacked and drove him off. The bandit chief Wang Wenjin styled himself Son of Heaven, held Dongyang, and appointed his follower Cai Daoren Minister of Works to guard Le'an, the record states. Su advanced to attack, the record states. He pacified them all alike. He also defeated the Yongjia bandit chief Shen Xiaoche, the record states. Then he marched overland toward Tiantai and directed his course at Linhai Commandery. He then captured fugitives; before and after more than a hundred battles, Zhihui fled and held out in Min-Yue, the record states. Because Su had long labored outside, an edict ordered him to enter court by relay post; his son Xuangan was given upper opening general and eight thousand lengths of brocade. Su, because remaining bandits were not yet destroyed and feared they would become a later trouble, again requested to go on campaign himself, the record states. An edict made Su field marshal; he again rode relay post to Kuaiji.
78
先是，泉州人王國慶，南安豪族也，殺刺史劉弘，據州為亂。 自以海路艱阻，非北人所習，不設備伍。 素泛海奄至，國慶遑遽，棄州走。 素分遣諸將，水陸追捕。 時南海先有五六百家，居水為亡命，號曰遊艇子； 智慧、國慶欲往依之。 素乃密令人說國慶，令斬智慧以自效。 因慶乃斬智慧於泉州。 自余支黨悉降，江南大定。 上遣左領軍將軍獨孤陀至浚儀迎勞，比到京師，問者日至。 拜素子玄獎儀同，賜黃金四十斤，加銀瓶，實以金錢，縑三千段、馬二百匹、羊三千口、田百頃、宅一區。
Earlier Wang Guoqing of Quanzhou, a powerful clan of Nan'an, had killed Regional Inspector Liu Hong and seized the province in rebellion, the record states. He considered the sea route difficult and treacherous and not what northerners were accustomed to, and did not set up defensive units, the record states. Su crossed the sea and suddenly arrived; Guoqing was flustered and abandoned the province and fled, the record states. Su dispatched the various generals to pursue by land and sea, the record states. At that time in Nanhai there were already five or six hundred households living on the water as fugitives, known as the Wandering Boat People; Zhihui and Guoqing wished to go and rely on them, the record states. Su therefore secretly sent someone to persuade Guoqing to kill Zhihui to prove his merit, the record states. Because of this Guoqing then beheaded Zhihui at Quanzhou, the record states. The remaining branches and factions all submitted; the Jiangnan region was greatly settled, the record states. The emperor sent Left Palace Commander Dugu Tuo to Junyi to welcome and reward him; by the time he reached the capital, visitors came daily to inquire, the record states. Su's son Xuanjiang was appointed honors equal; he was given forty jin of gold, with a silver bottle filled with gold coins added, three thousand bolts of silk, two hundred horses, three thousand sheep, a hundred qing of fields, and one residence.
