代蘇威為尚書右僕射，與高熲專掌朝政。 素性疏而辯，高下在心，朝貴之內，頗推高熲，敬牛弘，厚接薛道衡，視蘇威蔑如也。 自餘朝臣，多被陵轢。 其才藝風調，優於高熲。 至於推誠體國，處物平當，有宰相識度，不如熲遠矣。
He replaced Su Wei as right vice director of the Masters of Writing and with Gao Jiong exclusively managed court government. Su's nature was careless yet eloquent; high and low were in his heart; among the court nobility he fairly elevated Gao Jiong, respected Niu Hong, treated Xue Daoheng generously, and looked on Su Wei with contempt, the record states. The remaining court ministers were mostly bullied and insulted by him, the record states. In talent, artistry, and bearing he was superior to Gao Jiong, the record states. But in giving one's heart in sincerity and embodying the state, in handling things with fairness and balance, and in the discernment of a chief minister, he was far inferior to Jiong, the record states.
80
尋令素監營仁壽宮，素遂夷山堙穀，督役嚴急，作者多死，宮側時聞鬼哭。 及宮成，上令高熲前視，奏稱頗傷綺麗，大損人丁。 帝不悅。 素懼，即於北門啟獨孤皇后曰：「帝王法有離宮別館，今天下太平，造一宮何足損費。 」後以此理諭上，上乃解。 於是賜錢百萬、綿絹三千段。
Soon afterward he was ordered to supervise construction of Renshou Palace; Su then leveled mountains and filled valleys, supervising labor with harsh urgency; many workers died, and beside the palace one sometimes heard ghosts weeping, the record states. When the palace was completed, the emperor had Gao Jiong go to inspect it first; he reported that it was rather excessively ornate and had greatly wasted manpower, the record states. The emperor took displeasure. Su was afraid and immediately at the North Gate reported to Empress Dowager Dugu, saying, "The law of emperors and kings provides for detached palaces and separate halls; now the realm is at peace — building one palace can hardly be called wasting resources." The empress later used this reasoning to persuade the emperor, and the emperor then relented. Then he was given a million coins and three thousand lengths of cotton silk.
81
開皇十八年，突厥達頭可汗犯塞，以素為靈州道行軍總管。 出塞討之，賜物二千段、黃金百斤。 先是諸將與虜戰，每慮胡騎奔突，皆戎車步騎相參，與鹿角為方陣，騎在內。 素曰：「此乃自固之道。 」於是悉除舊法，令諸軍為騎陣。 達頭聞之，大喜，以為天賜，下馬仰天而拜，率精騎十餘萬至。 素奮擊，大破。 達頭被重創而遁，眾號哭而去。 優詔賜縑二萬匹及萬釘寶帶，加子玄感位大將軍，玄獎、玄縱、積善並上儀同。
In the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, Tardush Khan of the Turks invaded the frontier; Su was made field headquarters commander of the Lingzhou route. He went beyond the frontier to attack them and was given two thousand lengths of goods and a hundred jin of gold, the record states. Earlier when the generals fought the barbarians, they always feared the barbarian horsemen would charge; chariots, infantry, and cavalry were mixed together in a square formation with antlers, with the cavalry inside, the record states. Su said, "That is merely a way to defend oneself." Then he completely abolished the old methods and ordered all armies to form cavalry formations. When Tardush heard this he was greatly pleased, thinking it a gift from Heaven; he dismounted, bowed to Heaven, and came with more than a hundred thousand elite horsemen, the record states. Su struck vigorously and greatly defeated them, the record states. Tardush suffered heavy wounds and fled; his troops wailed and departed, the record states. A gracious edict gave twenty thousand bolts of silk and a precious belt studded with ten thousand nails; his son Xuangan was given the rank of general-in-chief, and Xuanjiang, Xuanzong, and Jishan were all given upper honors equal.
82
素多權略，乘機赴敵，應變無方。 然大抵馭戎嚴整，有犯令者，立斬無所寬貸。 每將臨寇，輒求人過失而斬之，多者百餘人，少不下數十，流血盈前，言笑自若。 及對陣，先令一二百人赴敵，陷陣則已，如不能陷而還，無問多少，悉斬之。 又令二百人復進，還如向法。 將士股栗，有必死心，由是戰無不勝，稱為名將。 素時貴幸，言無不從。 其從素征代者，微功必錄。 至於他將，雖大功，多為文吏所譴卻。 故素雖嚴忍，士亦以此願從。
Su had many stratagems; seizing opportunities to meet the enemy, he responded to changes without fixed method, the record states. Yet in general he controlled the army with strict order; those who violated commands were beheaded on the spot without leniency, the record states. Whenever he was about to face the enemy, he would seek men's faults and behead them — more than a hundred in some cases, never fewer than several dozen; blood filled the ground before him, yet he talked and laughed as if at ease, the record states. When facing battle, he first ordered one or two hundred men to charge the enemy; if they broke the formation that was that, but if they could not break through and returned, without asking how many, all were beheaded, the record states. He then ordered two hundred men to advance again; if they returned it was by the same rule, the record states. Officers and soldiers trembled in the thighs and had hearts resolved on death; because of this he was victorious in every battle and was called a famous general, the record states. Su at that time was favored and trusted; nothing he said went unheeded, the record states. Those who followed Su in campaigns against the northern barbarians had even slight merit recorded, the record states. As for other generals, even for great merit they were mostly rejected by the civil officials, the record states. Therefore although Su was harsh and cruel, soldiers for this reason were willing to follow him, the record states.
83
二十年，晉王廣為靈、朔道行軍元帥，素為長史，王卑躬交素。 及為太子，素之謀也。 仁壽初，代高熲為尚書左僕射，賜良馬十匹、牝馬二百匹、奴婢百口。 其年，以素為行軍元帥，出雲中擊突厥，連破之。 突厥走，追至夜及之。 將復戰，恐賊越逸，令其騎稍後，於是親將兩騎並降突厥二人與虜並行，不之覺也。 侯其頓舍未定，趣後騎掩擊，大破之。 自是突厥遠遁，磧南無復虜庭。 以功進子玄感位柱國，玄縱為淮南郡公，賞物二萬段。
In the twentieth year, Prince of Jin Guang was field marshal of the Ling and Shuo route mobile headquarters, and Su was chief clerk; the prince bowed humbly in treating Su. When he became crown prince, it was Su's plotting, the record states. At the beginning of Renshou he replaced Gao Jiong as left vice director of the Masters of Writing and was given ten fine horses, two hundred mares, and a hundred male and female servants. That year Su was made field marshal, went out from Yunzhong to attack the Turks, and defeated them repeatedly. The Turks fled; he pursued them and caught up by night, the record states. About to fight again, fearing the bandits would escape over the frontier, he ordered his cavalry to hang back; he personally led two horsemen together with two surrendered Turks to ride alongside the enemy without their noticing, the record states. Waiting until their camp was not yet settled, he urged the rear cavalry to strike by surprise and greatly defeated them, the record states. From this the Turks fled far away, and south of the desert there was no longer a barbarian court, the record states. For merit his son Xuangan's rank was advanced to pillar of state, Xuanzong was made Duke of Huainan, and he was given twenty thousand lengths of goods.
84
及獻皇后崩，山陵制度多出於素。 上善之，下詔曰：「君為元首，臣則股肱，共理百姓，義同一體。 上柱國、尚書左僕射、仁壽宮大監、越國公素，志度恢弘，機鑒明遠，懷佐時之略，包經國之才。 王業初基，霸圖肇建，策名委質，受脤出師，禽翦凶魁，克平虢、鄭。 頻承廟算，揚旌江表； 每稟戎律，長驅塞垣。 南指而吳越肅清，北臨而獯獫摧服。 自居端揆，參贊機衡，當朝正色，直言無隱。 論文則詞藻從橫，語武則權奇間出，既文且武，唯朕所命。 任使之處，夙夜無怠。 獻皇后奄離六宮，遠日雲及，塋兆安厝，委素經紀。 然葬事依禮，唯卜泉石，至如吉凶，不由於此。 素義存奉上，情深體國，欲使幽明俱泰，永保無窮。 以為陰陽之書，聖人所作，禍福之理，特須審慎。 乃遍曆川原，親自占擇，志圖元吉，孜孜不已。 遂得神皋福壤，營建山陵。 論素此心，事極誠孝，豈與平戎定寇，比其功業，若不加褒賞，何以申茲勸勵。 可別封一子義康郡公、邑萬戶，子子孫孫承襲不絕，餘如故。 」並賜田三十頃、絹萬匹、米萬石； 金缽一，實以金； 銀缽一，實以珠； 並綾錦五百段。
When Empress Dowager Xian died, the mountain tomb regulations mostly came from Su, the record states. The emperor approved and issued an edict saying, "The ruler is the head and ministers the arms and legs; together they govern the hundred surnames, their duty one body." Upper pillar of state, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, grand supervisor of Renshou Palace, Duke of Yue Su — his resolve and measure are broad, his insight clear and far-reaching; he holds strategies to assist the age and talent to manage the state. When the royal enterprise was first founded and the hegemonic design newly established, he registered his name and devoted his substance, received the sacrificial flesh and went out as commander, captured and cut down the fierce chiefs, and conquered and pacified Guo and Zheng, the record states. Again and again receiving the temple's calculations, he raised banners south of the Yangzi; Whenever he received military law he drove far along the frontier wall, the record states. Pointing south, Wu and Yue were cleared and pacified; facing north, the Xiongnu were broken and subdued, the record states. Once occupying the chief minister's seat, he assisted in the pivots of state, maintained upright color at court, and spoke directly without concealment, the record states. In literature his words were brilliant and unrestrained; in martial affairs his stratagems were singular and emerged at intervals — both literary and martial, exactly as I command, the record states. In the places where he is employed, he is never idle day or night, the record states. Empress Dowager Xian suddenly departed the six palaces; the distant day drew near, the tomb mound was settled and placed — all was entrusted to Su to manage, the record states. Yet burial affairs follow ritual — only spring stones are divined; as for fortune and misfortune, it does not depend on this, the record states. Su's righteousness lay in serving above, his feeling deep in embodying the state; he wished to make dark and bright both at peace and preserve them forever without end, the record states. He considered that books of yin and yang were made by sages, and the principles of fortune and misfortune must especially be carefully examined, the record states. He therefore went everywhere through rivers and plains, personally divining and selecting, striving for supreme good fortune, diligently without ceasing, the record states. He thus obtained divine highland and blessed soil and built the mountain tomb, the record states. Considering Su's heart in this matter, his conduct was extremely sincere and filial — how could that be compared with pacifying barbarians and settling bandits? If reward and praise are not added, how can such encouragement be expressed? One of his sons may separately be enfeoffed as Duke of Yikang with a fief of ten thousand households, to be inherited by sons and grandsons without end; the rest as before. He also received thirty qing of fields, ten thousand bolts of silk, and ten thousand shi of rice; a gold bowl filled with gold; a silver bowl filled with pearls; and five hundred lengths of damask and brocade, the record states.
85
時素貴寵日隆。 其弟約、從父文思、弟紀及族父異並尚書、列卿，諸子無汗馬勞，位柱國、刺史。 家僮數千，後庭妓妾曳綺羅者以千數； 第宅華侈，制擬宮禁。 有鮑亨者善屬文，殷胄者工草隸，並江南士人，因高智慧沒為奴。 親戚故吏，布列清顯。 其盛近古未聞。 煬帝初為太子，忌蜀王秀，與素謀之，構成其罪，後竟廢黜。 朝臣有違忤者，雖至誠體國如賀若弼、史萬歲、李綱、柳彧等，素皆陰中之。 若有附會及親戚，雖無才用，必加進擢。 朝廷靡然，莫不畏附。 唯兵部尚書柳述，以帝婿之重，數於上前面折素。 大理卿梁毗，抗表言素作威作福。 上漸疏忌之，後因出敕曰：「僕射，國之宰輔，不可躬親細務，但三五日一度向省評論大事。 」外示優崇，實奪之權，終仁壽之末，不復通判省事。 上賜王公已下射，素箭為第一，上手以外國所獻金精盤價直巨萬以賜之。 四年，從幸仁壽宮，宴賜重疊。
At that time Su's favor and privilege grew daily, the record states. His younger brother Yue, his father's younger cousin Wensi, his younger brother Ji, and his clan uncle Yi were all ministers and attendant-in-ordinary; his sons without sweat-and-horse merit held ranks of pillar of state and regional inspector. Household slaves numbered in the thousands; concubines and entertainers trailing gauze and silk also numbered in the thousands; Residences were luxurious and extravagant, modeled on the palace prohibitions, the record states. There were Bao Heng, skilled at composing prose, and Yin Zhou, adept at cursive and clerical script — both scholars of the Jiangnan region who because of Gao Zhihui had been taken as slaves, the record states. Relatives and former subordinates were spread among prominent posts, the record states. Such splendor had not been heard of in recent antiquity, the record states. When Emperor Yang had first been crown prince, he resented Prince of Shu Xiu; with Su he plotted and constructed his guilt, and in the end Xiu was deposed, the record states. Court ministers who opposed him — even those who gave their hearts in sincerity and embodied the state like He Ruo Bi, Shi Wansui, Li Gang, and Liu Yu — Su all secretly struck at them, the record states. If there were those who attached themselves to him or were kin, even without talent or ability, he certainly advanced and promoted them, the record states. The court leaned in submission; none did not fear and attach themselves, the record states. Only Minister of War Liu Shu, by weight of being the emperor's son-in-law, repeatedly rebuked Su before the emperor's face, the record states. Director of the Court of Justice Liang Pi submitted a memorial resisting Su for wielding authority and wielding favor, the record states. The emperor gradually grew distant and suspicious, and later issued an edict saying, "The vice director is the state's chief assistant and cannot personally attend to minor affairs — only once every three or five days come to the ministry to discuss great affairs." Outwardly showing superior honor, in reality stripping his power — by the end of Renshou he no longer jointly adjudicated ministry affairs, the record states. The emperor granted archery to kings and dukes downward; Su's arrow was first, and the emperor with his own hand gave him a golden essence dish from a foreign state worth tens of thousands, the record states. In the fourth year he followed the emperor's visit to Renshou Palace and received feasts and gifts in layers, the record states.
86
及上不豫，素與兵部尚書柳述、黃門侍郎元岩等入侍疾。 時皇太子入居大寶殿，慮上有不諱，須豫防擬，乃手自為書，封出問素。 素條錄事狀，以報太子。 宮人潛送於上，上覽而大恚。 所寵陳貴人又言太子無禮。 上遂發怒，欲召庶人勇。 太子謀之素，素矯詔追東宮兵士帖上臺宿衛，門禁出入，並取宇文述、郭衍節度。 又令張衡侍疾。 上以此日崩，由是頗有異論。
When the emperor fell ill, Su together with minister of war Liu Shu, attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate Yuan Yan, and others entered to attend the illness. At that time the crown prince entered and resided in the Great Treasure Hall; fearing the emperor might have an unfavorable turn, he needed to prepare defenses in advance, and personally wrote a letter, sealed it, and sent it out to ask Su, the record states. Su listed the circumstances item by item and reported to the crown prince, the record states. A palace woman secretly sent it to the emperor; the emperor read it and was greatly enraged, the record states. The favored Lady Chen also said the crown prince was disrespectful, the record states. The emperor then grew angry and wished to summon the commoner Yong. The crown prince plotted with Su; Su forged an edict to recall Eastern Palace soldiers to garrison the upper platform in night watch; entry and exit at the gates were all taken under the command of Yuwen Shu and Guo Yan, the record states. He also ordered Zhang Heng to attend the illness, the record states. The emperor died on that day; because of this there were rather differing opinions, the record states.
87
會漢王諒反，遣茹茹天保往東蒲州，燒斷河橋，又遣王𨈭子並力拒守。 素將輕騎五千襲之。 潛於渭口宵濟，比明擊之。 天保敗，𨈭子懼，以城降。 有詔征還。 初素將行，計日破賊，皆如所量。 帝於是以素為并州道行軍總管、河北道安撫大使，討諒。 時晉、絳、呂三州並為諒城守，素各以二千人縻之而去。 諒遣趙子開擁眾十餘萬，築絕徑路，屯據高壁，佈陣五十里。 素令諸將以兵臨之，自以奇兵深入霍山，緣崖谷而進，直指其營，一戰破之，諒所署介州刺史梁修羅屯介休，聞素至，懼，棄城而走。 進至清源，去并州三十里。 率其將王世宗、趙子開、蕭摩訶等來拒戰，又擊破之，禽蕭摩訶。 退保并州，素進兵圍之。 諒窮而降，餘黨悉平。 帝遣素弟修武公約齎手詔勞，素上表陳謝。 其月，還京師。 從駕幸洛陽，以素領營東京大監。 以平諒功，拜其子萬石、仁行、侄玄挺皆儀同三司，賚物五萬段、羅綺千匹、諒之妓妾二十人。 大業元年，遷尚書令賜東京甲第一區、物二千段，尋拜太師，餘官如故。 前後賞錫不可勝計。 明年，拜司徒，改封楚公，真食二千五百戶。 其年病薨，諡曰景武。 贈光祿大夫、太尉公、弘農河東絳郡臨汾文城河內汲郡長平上黨河十郡太守，給轀輬車、班劍三十人、前後部羽葆鼓吹、粟麥五千石、物五千段，鴻臚監護喪事。 帝又下詔立碑，以彰盛美。 素嘗以五言詩七百字贈番州刺史薛道衡，詞氣穎拔，風韻秀上，為一時盛作。 未幾而卒，道衡歎曰：「人之將死，其言也善，若是乎！ 」《集》十卷。
When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, he sent Ruru Tianbao to Dongpu Province to burn and break the river bridge, and also sent Wang Kui and others together to resist and hold, the record states. Su led five thousand light horsemen to strike them, the record states. He secretly crossed at night at Wei Ford; by dawn he attacked, the record states. Tianbao was defeated; Kui was afraid and surrendered the city, the record states. An edict ordered him recalled, the record states. When Su was about to go, he calculated the days to defeat the bandits, and all matched his reckoning, the record states. The emperor therefore made Su field headquarters commander of the Bingzhou route and pacification commissioner of the Hebei route to attack Liang. At that time Jin, Jiang, and Lü, the three provinces, all held out for Liang; Su tied down each with two thousand men and departed, the record states. Liang sent Zhao Zikai with more than a hundred thousand troops, building to cut off the narrow path, stationed holding the high ramparts, arraying troops for fifty li, the record states. Su ordered the generators to press them with troops; he himself with elite troops went deep into Huo Mountain, followed cliff valleys and advanced, pointing straight at their camp, and broke them in one battle. Liang's appointed regional inspector of Jiezhou Liang Xiuluo garrisoned Jiexiu; hearing Su had arrived, he was afraid and abandoned the city and fled. Advancing to Qingyuan, thirty li from Bing Province, the record states. Liang's generals Wang Shizong, Zhao Zikai, Xiao Mohe, and others came to resist in battle; he again attacked and defeated them and captured Xiao Mohe, the record states. They retreated to hold Bing Province; Su advanced and besieged it, the record states. Liang was driven to extremity and surrendered; the remaining factions were all pacified, the record states. The emperor sent Su's younger brother Duke of Xiuwu Yue bearing an imperial letter by hand to reward him; Su submitted a memorial of thanks, the record states. That month he returned to the capital, the record states. Following the emperor's visit to Luoyang, Su was appointed grand supervisor of the Eastern Capital camp. For merit in pacifying Liang, his sons Wanshi and Renxing and nephew Xuanting were all made honors equal to the three excellencies; he was given fifty thousand lengths of goods, a thousand bolts of silk gauze, and twenty of Liang's concubines and entertainers. In the first year of Daye he was transferred to minister over the Masters of Writing and given one first-rank residence in the Eastern Capital and two thousand lengths of goods; soon afterward he was appointed grand preceptor, his other offices as before. Rewards and gifts before and after were beyond counting, the record states. The next year he was appointed minister over the masses, his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Chu, with a true fief of twenty-five hundred households. That year he died of illness; his posthumous name was Jingwu (Stern and Martial). Posthumously he was honored as grand master of splendid happiness, Duke of Grand Guardian, grand administrator of the ten commanderies of Hongnong, Hedong, Jiang, Fen, Wen, Cheng, Henei, Ji, Changping, Shangdang, and He, given a funeral carriage, thirty guards with swords, feathered parasols and drums before and behind, five thousand shi of millet and wheat, and five thousand lengths of goods; the supervisor of guests supervised the funeral rites. The emperor also issued an edict to erect a stele to display the splendid beauty, the record states. Su once gave a five-character poem of seven hundred characters to Regional Inspector of Fanzhou Xue Daoheng; the wording was sharp and elevated, the tone elegant and superior — a masterpiece of the age. Before long he was dead; Daoheng sighed and said, "When a man is about to die, his words are good — is it like this!" Collected Works, ten juan.
88
素雖有建立策及平楊諒功，然特為帝猜忌，外示殊禮，內情甚薄。 太史言楚分野有大喪，因改封素于楚。 寢疾之日，帝每令名醫診侯，賜以上藥； 然密問醫人，恆恐不死。 素又自知名位已極，不肯服藥，變不將慎。 每語弟約曰：「我豈須更活邪？」
Although Su had achievements in founding strategies and merit in pacifying Yang Liang, yet the emperor was especially suspicious of him; outwardly showing special courtesy, inwardly his feeling was very thin, the record states. The grand astrologer said the Chu asterism's territory would suffer a great mourning; therefore Su's enfeoffment was changed to Chu. During his illness the emperor each day ordered famous physicians to examine him and gave him the finest medicines; Yet secretly he asked the physicians, always fearing Su would not die, the record states. Su also knew himself that fame and rank had reached their limit and refused to take medicine, no longer exercising caution, the record states. He often told his younger brother Yue, "Do I still need to live? — so he said."
89
素貪財貨，營求產業，東西京居宅侈麗，朝毀夕復，營繕無已。 爰及諸方都會之處，邸店水磑田宅以千百數。 時議以此鄙之。 子玄感。
Su was greedy for wealth and goods, scheming for property; residences in the eastern and western capitals were luxurious and splendid, destroyed in the morning and rebuilt in the evening, construction without end, the record states. Extending to all major cities of the regions, inns, water mills, fields, and residences numbered in the hundreds and thousands, the record states. Public opinion therefore despised him. His son was Xuangan.
90
玄感少時晚成，人多謂之癡。 唯素每謂所親曰：「此兒不癡也。 」及長，美須髯，儀貌雄俊，好讀書，便騎射。 弱冠，以父軍功位柱國，與其父俱為第二品，朝會則齊列。 後文帝命玄感降一等，玄感拜謝曰：「不意陛下寵臣之甚，許以公庭獲展私敬。 」初拜郢州刺史，到官潛布耳目，察長吏能不，纖介必知，吏人敬服，皆稱其能。 後轉宋州刺史，父憂去職。 歲餘，拜鴻臚卿，襲爵楚公，遷禮部尚書。 性雖驕居，而愛重文學，四海知名之士多趨其門。
Xuangan in youth matured late; many people called him dull, the record states. Only Su often told those close to him, "This boy is no dullard." When grown he had a fine beard and mustache, a heroic and handsome appearance, loved reading books, and was skilled at mounted archery, the record states. At the capping age, because of his father's military merit he held the rank of pillar of state; he and his father both held the second rank and at court assemblies stood in the same row. Later Emperor Wen ordered Xuangan reduced one rank; Xuangan bowed in thanks and said, "I did not expect Your Majesty to favor me so greatly as to permit private respect in the public court." When first appointed regional inspector of Yingzhou, upon reaching his post he secretly deployed informants to observe whether the senior officials were capable; the slightest detail he always knew; officials and people respected and submitted, all calling him capable. Later he was transferred to regional inspector of Songzhou and left office for his father's mourning. After more than a year he was appointed supervisor of guests, inherited the dukedom of Chu, and was transferred to minister of rites. Although his nature was proud in station, he valued and honored literature; renowned scholars of the four seas mostly hastened to his gate, the record states.
91
後見朝綱漸紊，帝又猜忌日甚，內不自安，遂與諸弟潛謀廢帝立秦王浩。 及從征吐谷渾，還至達鬥拔谷，時從官狼狽，玄感欲襲擊行宮。 其叔慎曰：「士心尚一，國未有釁，不可圖也。 」玄感乃止。 時帝好征伐，玄感欲立威名，陰求將領，以告兵部尚書段文振。 振以白帝，帝嘉之，謂群臣曰：「將門有將，故不虛也。 」於是賚物千段，禮遇益隆，頗預朝政。
Later seeing court discipline gradually disordered and the emperor's suspicion growing daily, inwardly he was not at ease and therefore with his younger brothers secretly plotted to depose the emperor and install Prince of Qin Hao, the record states. When he followed the campaign against Tuyuhun and returned to Databagu, at that time the attendant officials were in disorder and Xuangan wished to strike the traveling palace, the record states. His uncle Shen said, "Men's hearts are still united and the state has no crack — this cannot be plotted." Xuangan then stopped. At that time the emperor loved campaigns; Xuangan wished to establish a martial reputation and secretly sought generals, telling Minister of War Duan Wenzhen, the record states. Wenzhen reported it to the emperor; the emperor commended him and told the ministers, "A general's house produces generals — the saying is not empty." Then he was given a thousand lengths of goods; courtesy and favor grew ever greater, and he fairly participated in court government.
92
帝征遼東，令玄感黎陽督運。 遂與武賁郎將王仲伯、汲郡贊治趙懷義等謀，不時進發。 帝遣使者逼促，玄感揚言曰：「水路多盜，不可前後而發。 」其弟武賁郎將玄縱、鷹揚郎將萬石並從幸遼東，玄感潛遣人召之。 時來護兒以舟師自東萊，將入海趣平壤城，軍未發。 玄感無以動眾，乃遣家奴偽為使，從東方來，謬稱護失軍期而反。 玄感遂入黎陽縣，閉城大募勇夫。 於是取颿布為牟甲，署置官屬皆准開皇之舊。 移書傍郡以討護為名，令發兵會於倉所。 以東光縣尉元務本為黎州刺史，趙懷義為衛州刺史，河內郡主簿唐禕為懷州刺史，有眾且一萬，將襲洛陽。 唐禕至河內，馳往東都告之。 越王侗、戶部尚書樊子蓋等勒兵備禦。 修武縣人相率守臨清關，玄感不得濟，遂于汲郡南度河。 從亂如市，數日，屯兵上春門，眾至十餘萬。 子蓋令河南贊務裴弘策拒之，弘策戰敗，父老競致牛酒。 玄感屯兵尚書省，每有誓眾曰：「我身為上柱國，家累巨萬金，至富貴，無所求也。 今者不顧破家滅族者，為天下解倒懸之急，救黎元之命耳。 」眾皆悅，詣轅門請自效者日數千。 及與樊子蓋書曰：
When the emperor campaigned against Liaodong, he ordered Xuangan to supervise transport at Liyang, the record states. He then plotted with Brave Guard attendant Wang Zhongbo, assistant administrator of Ji Commandery Zhao Huaiyi, and others not to advance on schedule. The emperor sent envoys to press him urgently; Xuangan proclaimed publicly, "There are many bandits on the water route — the front and rear cannot depart together." His younger brothers brave guard attendant Xuanzong and hawkish guard attendant Wanshi were both following the emperor's visit to Liaodong; Xuangan secretly sent men to summon them. At that time Lai Huer with the fleet from Donglai was about to enter the sea and hurry to Pyongyang; the army had not yet set out, the record states. Xuangan had no means to move the masses; he therefore sent a household slave disguised as an envoy from the east to falsely say Huer had missed the army deadline and rebelled, the record states. Xuangan then entered Liyang County, closed the gates, and greatly recruited brave men, the record states. Then he took sailcloth for armor and appointed officials all according to the Kaihuang precedent. He sent letters to neighboring commanderies in the name of attacking Huer, ordering them to send troops to assemble at the granary, the record states. He made Dongguang County lieutenant Yuan Wuben regional inspector of Li Province, Zhao Huaiyi regional inspector of Wei Province, and Henei commandery registrar Tang Yi regional inspector of Huai Province; with troops nearly ten thousand he was about to strike Luoyang. When Tang Yi reached Henei he galloped to the eastern capital to report it, the record states. Prince of Yue Tong, Minister of Revenue Fan Zigai, and others mustered troops to defend, the record states. The people of Xiuwu County together held Linqing Pass; Xuangan could not cross and therefore crossed the river south of Ji Commandery, the record states. Those who followed the disorder were like a market; within several days he stationed troops at Shangchun Gate; the masses reached more than a hundred thousand, the record states. Zigai ordered Henan assistant administrator Pei Hongce to resist him; Hongce was defeated in battle, and elders competed to present oxen and wine. Xuangan stationed troops at the Ministry of the Masters of Writing; whenever he rallied the masses he said, "I myself am an upper pillar of state; my family accumulates tens of thousands in gold — I have reached the utmost in wealth and rank and want nothing more." Now I disregard the destruction of family and clan because the realm hangs upside down in urgent peril and the lives of the black-haired people must be saved, the record states. The masses were all pleased; those who came to the camp gate daily requesting to serve numbered in the thousands, the record states. In his letter to Fan Zigai he wrote:
93
夫建忠立義，事有多途，見機而作，蓋非一揆。 昔伊尹放太甲于桐宮，霍光廢劉賀於昌邑，此並公度內，不能一二披陳。 高祖文皇帝誕膺天命，造茲區宇，在ＦＭ璣以齊七政，握金鏡以馭六龍，無為而至化流，垂拱而天下乂。 今上纂承寶曆，宜固洪基，乃自絕於天，殄人敗德。 頻年肆眚，盜賤於是滋多； 所在修營，人力為之凋盡。 荒淫酒色，子女必被其侵； 耽玩鷹犬，禽獸皆離其毒。 朋黨相扇，貸賄公行，納邪佞之言，杜正直之口。 加以轉輸不息，徭役無期； 士卒填溝壑，骸骨蔽原野； 黃河之北則千里無煙，江、淮之間則鞠為茂草。
Establishing loyalty and righteousness has many paths; seizing opportunity and acting is surely not one measure alone, the record states. In old times Yi Yin placed Tai Jia in the Tong Palace and Huo Guang deposed Liu He in Changyi — these were all within public measure and cannot be fully set forth one by one, the record states. High Ancestor Emperor Wen received Heaven's mandate and created this realm; he aligned the celestial pearl to harmonize the seven regulators and grasped the golden mirror to drive the six dragons — through non-action transformation flowed, through draped sleeves the realm was governed, the record states. The present ruler inherits the precious succession and should consolidate the great foundation, yet he himself cuts off from Heaven and destroys men and ruins virtue, the record states. Year after year he grants amnesties, and bandits therefore grow more numerous; wherever construction is undertaken, human strength is exhausted to the last, the record states. Indulging in debauchery, wine, and women — daughters must suffer his advances; addicted to hawks and dogs — birds and beasts all suffer his poison, the record states. Factions fan one another; bribes walk openly; he accepts the words of the wicked and flatterers and stops the mouths of the upright, the record states. Added to this, transport and relay never cease and corvée labor has no end; soldiers fill ditches and gullies while bones cover the open fields; north of the Yellow River for a thousand li there is no smoke; between the Yangzi and Huai it has become luxuriant grass, the record states.
94
玄感世荷國恩，位居上將。 先公奉遺詔曰：「好子孫為我輔弼之，惡子孫為我屏黜之。 」所以上稟先旨，下順人心，廢此淫昏，更立明哲。 今四海同心，九有咸應，士卒用命，如赴私仇，人庶相趨，義形公道。 天意人事，較然可知。 公獨害孤城，勢何支久？ 願以黔黎在念，社稷為心，勿拘小禮，自貽伊戚。 誰謂國家，一旦至此！ 執筆潸然，言無所具。
Xuangan for generations has received the state's grace and occupies the rank of upper general, the record states. My late father received the deathbed edict: "Good sons and grandsons — make them my assistants; wicked sons and grandsons — make them my screen and remove them." Therefore above I uphold the late intent, below I follow men's hearts, deposing this debauched ruler and installing another wise and bright one, the record states. Now the four seas share one heart and the nine regions all respond; soldiers obey orders as if answering a private feud; people and commoners hurry together, righteousness taking the form of public duty, the record states. Heaven's intent and men's affairs — compared, they are clearly knowable, the record states. You alone harm this isolated city — how long can you hold out? I wish you would keep the black-haired people in mind and take the altars of state to heart; do not be bound by minor ritual and bring this grief upon yourself, the record states. Who would have thought the state would one day come to this! Taking up the brush with tears streaming, words cannot fully express, the record states.
95
遂進逼東都城。 刑部尚書衛玄率眾自關中來援東都，以步騎二萬度瀍、澗挑戰。 玄感偽北，玄逐之，伏兵發，前軍盡沒。 後數日，玄復與玄感戰。 兵始合，玄感詐令人大呼曰：「官軍已得玄感矣。 」玄軍稍怠，玄感與數千騎乘之，大潰，擁八千人而去。 玄感驍勇多力，每戰，親運長矛，身先士卒，喑鳴叱吒，所當莫不震懾，論者方之項羽。 又善撫馭，士樂致死。 由是戰無不捷。 玄軍日蹙，糧又盡，乃悉眾決戰，陣於北邙，一日間戰十餘合。 玄感弟玄挺中流矢而斃，玄感稍卻。 樊子蓋復遣兵攻尚書省，又殺數百人。
He then advanced and pressed the eastern capital city, the record states. Minister of Punishments Wei Xuan led troops from Guanzhong to rescue the eastern capital and with twenty thousand foot and horse soldiers crossed Chan and Jian to challenge battle, the record states. Xuangan feigned retreat north; Xuan pursued him; ambush troops sprang up and the vanguard was entirely destroyed, the record states. Several days later Xuan again fought Xuangan, the record states. As the armies were just joining battle, Xuangan had someone shout loudly, "The official army has already captured Xuangan!" Xuan's army slackened slightly; Xuangan with several thousand horsemen charged them and they were greatly routed; he drove off eight thousand men, the record states. Xuangan was fierce and brave with great strength; in every battle he personally wielded the long spear and led from the front, roaring and shouting; none who faced him did not tremble in awe; commentators compared him to Xiang Yu, the record states. He was also skilled at comforting and controlling; soldiers gladly died for him, the record states. Because of this he was victorious in every battle, the record states. Xuan's army was daily pressed; grain was also exhausted; he therefore gathered all troops for a decisive battle and arrayed at Beimang; in one day they fought more than ten engagements, the record states. Xuangan's younger brother Xuanting was struck by a flying arrow and died; Xuangan retreated somewhat, the record states. Fan Zigai again sent troops to attack the Ministry of the Masters of Writing and killed several hundred more, the record states.
96
帝遣武賁郎將陳稜攻元務本于黎陽。 武衛將軍屈突通屯河陽，左翊衛大將軍宇文述發兵繼進，右驍衛大將軍來護兒復來趙援。 玄感與前戶部尚書李子雄計曰：「屈突通曉兵事，若度河則勝負難決，不如分兵拒之。 不能濟，則樊、衛失援。 」玄感然之，將拒通。 子蓋知其謀，數擊其營，玄感不果進。 通遂濟河，軍於破陵。 玄感為兩軍，西拒衛玄，東拒屈突通。 子蓋復出兵大戰，玄感軍頻北。 復與子雄計，子雄勸之直入關中，開永豐倉振貧乏，三輔可指麾而定。 據有府庫，東面而爭天下，此亦霸王之業。
The emperor sent brave guard attendant Chen Leng to attack Yuan Wuben at Liyang. General of the martial guard Qu Tu Tong garrisoned Heyang; left assistant guard grand general Yuwen Shu launched troops in continued advance; right agile guard grand general Lai Huer also came from Zhao to reinforce. Xuangan plotted with former minister of revenue Li Zixiong, saying, "Qu Tu Tong understands military affairs; if he crosses the river then victory and defeat will be hard to decide — better to divide troops to resist him." If he cannot cross, then Fan and Wei lose support, the record states. Xuangan agreed and was about to resist Tong, the record states. Zigai knew his plan and repeatedly struck his camp; Xuangan could not advance as planned, the record states. Tong then crossed the river and encamped at Poling. Xuangan made two armies, resisting Wei Xuan in the west and Qu Tu Tong in the east, the record states. Zigai again sent troops for a great battle; Xuangan's army repeatedly retreated north, the record states. He again plotted with Zixiong; Zixiong urged him to enter Guanzhong directly, open the Yongfeng granary to relieve the poor, and the three auxiliaries could be commanded at a gesture, the record states. Holding the treasuries and storehouses and facing east to contend for the realm — this too is the enterprise of a hegemon, the record states.
97
會華陰諸楊請為鄉導，玄感遂釋洛陽，西圖關中。 宣言已破東都，取關西。 宇文述等諸軍躡之。 至弘農宮，父老遮說玄感曰：「宮城空虛，又多積粟，攻之易下。 進可絕敵人之食，退可割宜陽之地。 」玄感以為然，留攻三日，城不下，追兵遂至。 玄感西至閿鄉，上槃豆，佈陣亙五十里，與官軍且戰且行，一日三敗。 復陣于董杜原，諸軍大敗之。 玄感獨與十餘騎竄林木間，將奔上洛。 追騎至，玄感叱之，皆懼而返走。 至葭蘆戍，窘迫，獨與弟積善步行，謂積善曰：「事敗矣，我不能受人戮辱，汝可殺我。 」積善殺之，因自刺不死，為追兵所執，與玄感首俱送行在所，磔其屍於東都市，三日，復臠而焚之。 餘黨悉平。
When the Yang clan of Huayin requested to serve as local guides, Xuangan then released Luoyang and turned west to aim at Guanzhong. He proclaimed that he had already broken the eastern capital and was taking Guanxi, the record states. Yuwen Shu and the other armies pursued him, the record states. When they reached Hongnong Palace, elders blocked the way and told Xuangan, "The palace walls are empty and grain is greatly stored — attacking it is easy to take, the record states. Advancing you can cut off the enemy's food; retreating you can seize the land of Yiyang, the record states. Xuangan thought it correct and stayed to attack for three days; the city did not fall and pursuing troops then arrived, the record states. Xuangan went west to Wenxiang, ascended Pandou, and arrayed troops extending fifty li; with the official army he fought while marching and in one day was defeated three times, the record states. He again arrayed at Dongdu Plain; the various armies greatly defeated him, the record states. Xuangan alone with more than ten horsemen fled into the forest; he was about to flee to Shangluo, the record states. When pursuing horsemen arrived, Xuangan shouted at them and all feared and turned back to flee, the record states. When he reached Jialu Post he was hard pressed; alone with his younger brother Jishan he walked and said to Jishan, "The affair has failed — I cannot suffer the humiliation of being executed by others; you may kill me." Jishan killed him, then stabbed himself but did not die and was seized by pursuing troops; together with Xuangan's head he was sent to the traveling palace; his corpse was dismembered at the eastern capital market, and after three days was again cut to pieces and burned, the record states. The remaining factions were all subdued.
98
其弟玄獎為義陽太守，將歸玄感，為郡丞周旋玉所殺。 玄縱弟萬石，自帝所逃歸，至高陽，止傳舍，監事許華與郡兵執之，斬於涿郡。 萬石弟仁行，官至朝議大夫，斬于長安。 並具梟磔。 公卿請改玄感姓為梟氏，詔可之。
His younger brother Xuanjiang was grand administrator of Yiyang; about to return to Xuangan, he was killed by assistant administrator Zhou Xuan of the commandery. Xuanzong's younger brother Wanshi fled from the emperor's entourage and returned; reaching Gaoyang he stopped at a relay station; supervisor Xu Hua with commandery troops seized him and beheaded him in Zhuo commandery. Wanshi's younger brother Renxing, who had attained the rank of remonstrance and discussion grandee, was beheaded at Chang'an. All were fully dismembered and exposed, the record states. The kings and dukes requested changing Xuangan's surname to the Owl clan; an edict approved it, the record states.
99
玄感之亂，有趙元淑者預謀，誅。 又有劉元進，亦舉兵應之。
In Xuangan's rebellion there was one Zhao Yuanshu who participated in the plot and was executed, the record states. There was also Liu Yuanjin, who likewise raised troops in response, the record states.
100
元淑，博陵人。 父世模，初從高寶，後以眾歸周，授上開府，寓居京兆之雲陽。 隋文帝踐阼，恆典宿衛。 後從晉王伐陳，力戰而死。 朝廷以其身死王事，以元淑襲父本官，賜物三千段。 元淑性疏誕，不事產業，家徒壁立。 後授驃騎將軍，將之官，無以自給。 時長安富人宗連家累千金，仕周為三原令，有季女，慧而有色。 連每求賢夫，聞元淑，請與相見。 連有風儀，美談笑，元淑亦慕之。 及至其家，服玩居處，擬於將相，酒酣，奏女樂，元淑所未見也。 及出，連又致殷勤。 元淑再三來，宴樂更侈於前。 因問所須，盡買與之，元淑致謝，連復拜求以女妻之。 元淑感而納焉，遂為富人。
Yuanshu was a man of Boling, the record states. His father Shimu at first followed Gao Bao, then with his troops submitted to Zhou and was appointed upper opening general, residing in Yunyang of Jingzhao. When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he constantly held night watch in the palace guard, the record states. Later he followed the Prince of Jin in attacking Chen and died fighting bitterly, the record states. The court because he died in the king's service had Yuanshu inherit his father's former office and gave three thousand lengths of goods, the record states. Yuanshu's nature was careless and unrestrained; he did not manage property; his household was bare as a wall, the record states. Later he was appointed general of agile cavalry and was about to take up office but had no means to support himself. At that time the rich man of Chang'an Zong Lian's family accumulated thousands in gold; he had served Zhou as magistrate of Sanyuan and had a youngest daughter, clever and beautiful. Lian repeatedly sought a worthy son-in-law; hearing of Yuanshu he requested a meeting, the record states. Lian had bearing and grace and spoke elegantly; Yuanshu also admired him, the record states. When he reached his house, clothing, playthings, dwelling, and surroundings rivaled those of generals and ministers; when the wine was deep, female musicians performed — something Yuanshu had never seen, the record states. When he left, Lian again showed great cordiality, the record states. Yuanshu came again several times; feasts and music were even more extravagant than before, the record states. He therefore asked what was needed and bought everything for him; Yuanshu expressed thanks, and Lian again bowed requesting to give him his daughter in marriage, the record states. Yuanshu was moved and accepted her, and thereby became a rich man, the record states.
101
從楊素平楊諒，以功進位柱國，曆德州刺史、潁川太守，並有威惠。 入為司農卿。 玄感有異志，遂與結交。 遼東之役，領將軍、典宿衛，加光祿大夫，封葛國公。 明年，帝復征高麗，以元淑鎮監渝。 及玄感作亂，其弟玄縱自駕所逃歸，路經臨渝。 元淑出其小妻魏氏見玄縱，對宴極歡，因與通謀，並受玄縱賂遺。 及玄感敗，人有告其事者，帝以屬吏，元淑及魏氏俱斬於涿郡，籍沒其家。
Following Yang Su in pacifying Yang Liang, for merit his rank was advanced to pillar of state; he passed through regional inspector of Dezhou and grand administrator of Yingchuan, all with authority and kindness. He entered court as minister of agriculture. Xuangan had rebellious intent and therefore formed friendship with him, the record states. In the Liaodong campaign he led generals and held night watch in the palace guard, with the added rank of grand master of splendid happiness and enfeoffment as Duke of Ge State. The next year the emperor again campaigned against Goguryeo and made Yuanshu garrison and supervise Linyu, the record states. When Xuangan rebelled, his younger brother Xuanzong fled from the imperial carriage and returned; on the road he passed Linyu, the record states. Yuanshu brought out his concubine Lady Wei to meet Xuanzong; they feasted together in extreme merriment and therefore plotted together, both accepting bribes from Xuanzong, the record states. When Xuangan was defeated someone reported the matter; the emperor turned him over to the officials; Yuanshu and Lady Wei were both beheaded in Zhuo commandery and their property was confiscated.
102
元進，余杭人。 少好任俠，為州裏所宗，兩手各長尺餘，臂垂過膝。 屬遼東之役，百姓騷動，元進自以相表非常，遂聚亡命。 會玄感起于黎陽，元進應之。 旬月，眾至數萬，將度江而玄感敗。 吳郡硃燮、晉陵管崇亦舉兵，有眾七萬，共迎元進，奉以為主。 據吳郡，稱為天子，以燮、崇俱為僕射，署百官。 帝令將軍吐萬緒、光祿大夫魚俱羅討焉。 為緒所敗，硃燮戰死。 俄而緒、俱羅並得罪。 江都郡丞王世充發兵擊之。 有大流星墜于江都，未及地而南逝，磨拂竹木皆有聲，至吳郡而落於地。 元進惡之，令掘地入二丈得一石，徑丈餘。 數日，失石所在。 世充度江，元進遣兵人各持茅，因風縱火。 世充大懼，將棄營。 遇反風火轉，元進眾懼燒而退，世充大破之。 元進及崇俱為世充所殺。 世充坑其眾于黃亭澗，死者三萬人。 其後董道沖、沈法興、李子通等並乘此而起。 素母弟約。
Yuanjin was a man of Yuhang, the record states. From youth he loved chivalry and was honored by his district; each hand was more than a foot long and his arms hung past his knees, the record states. During the Liaodong campaign the common people were disturbed; Yuanjin considered his physiognomy extraordinary and therefore gathered fugitives, the record states. When Xuangan rose at Liyang, Yuanjin responded to him, the record states. Within ten days and a month the masses reached tens of thousands; he was about to cross the river when Xuangan was defeated, the record states. Zhu Xie of Wu commandery and Guan Chong of Jinling also raised troops with a force of seventy thousand; together they welcomed Yuanjin and installed him as leader. Holding Wu commandery he styled himself Son of Heaven; he made Xie and Chong both vice directors and appointed the hundred officials. The emperor ordered General Tuwann Xu and grand master of splendid happiness Yu Juluo to attack them. Xu defeated him; Zhu Xie died in battle. Before long both Xu and Juluo were condemned for offenses, the record states. Assistant administrator of Jiangdu commandery Wang Shichong launched troops to attack them. A great meteor fell at Jiangdu; before reaching the ground it sped south, grinding bamboo and trees with a sound all the way, and fell to earth at Wu commandery. Yuanjin hated this and ordered the ground dug two zhang deep, obtaining a stone more than a zhang in diameter, the record states. Several days later the stone's whereabouts were lost, the record states. Shichong crossed the river; Yuanjin sent soldiers each holding straw and, using the wind, set fires, the record states. Shichong was greatly afraid and was about to abandon the camp, the record states. Meeting a reverse wind the fire turned; Yuanjin's masses feared being burned and retreated; Shichong greatly defeated them, the record states. Yuanjin and Chong were both killed by Shichong, the record states. Shichong buried the dead in a pit at Huangting Stream; the dead numbered thirty thousand. Afterward Dong Daochong, Shen Faxiang, Li Zitong, and others all took advantage of this to rise, the record states. Su's younger brother by the same mother was Yue, the record states.
103
約字惠伯。 童兒時嘗登樹，墜地為查傷，由是竟為宦者。 性如沈靜，內多譎詐，好學強記。 素友愛之，凡有所為，先籌於約而行。 在周末，以素軍功賜爵安成縣公，拜上儀同三司。 文帝受禪，歷位長秋卿、鄜州刺史、宗正、大理三少卿。
Yue, styled Huibo. As a child he once climbed a tree, fell to the ground, and was injured by a branch; because of this he ended up a eunuch, the record states. His nature was deep and quiet, inwardly much deceitful; he loved learning and had a strong memory, the record states. Su loved and trusted him; whatever he undertook he first planned with Yue before acting, the record states. At the end of Zhou he because of Su's military merit was ennobled baron of Ancheng and appointed upper honors equal to the three excellencies. When Emperor Wen received the abdication he passed through the posts of director of the palace women's bureau, regional inspector of Fuzhou, director of the imperial clan, and three vice directors of the court of justice.
104
時皇太子無寵，晉王廣規奪宗，以素幸於上而雅信約，乃用張衡計，遣宇文述大以金寶賂約，因通王意，說之曰：「夫守正履道，固人臣之常致； 反經合義，亦達者之令圖。 自古賢人君子，莫不與時消息，以避禍患。 公兄弟功名蓋世，用事有年，朝臣為足下家所屈辱者，可勝數哉？ 又儲宮以所欲不行，每切齒於執政。 公雖自結於人主，而欲危公者亦多矣。 主上一旦棄群臣，公亦何以取庇？ 今皇太子失愛于皇后，主上素有廢黜之心，此公所知也。 今若請立晉王，在賢兄之口耳。 誠能因此時建大功，王必鎮銘於骨髓，斯則去累卵之危，成太山之安也。 」約然之，又白素。 素本凶險，聞之大喜，乃撫掌曰：「吾智慧殊不及此，賴汝起餘。 」約知其計行，復謂素曰：「今皇后之言，上無不用，宜因機會，早自結托，則匪惟長保榮祿，傳祚子孫。 又晉王傾身禮士，聲名日盛； 躬履節儉，有主上之風。 以約料之，必能安天下。 兄若遲疑，一旦有變，令太子用事，恐禍至無日。 」素遂行其策，太子果廢。
At that time the crown prince had no favor; the Prince of Jin Guang plotted to seize the succession; because Su was favored by the emperor and deeply trusted Yue, he used Zhang Heng's plan and sent Yuwen Shu with great gold and jewels to bribe Yue, thereby conveying the prince's intent and persuading him, saying, "Upholding correctness and treading the Way is the constant attainment of a minister; Going against the canon and joining with righteousness is also the excellent design of the far-sighted, the record states. Since ancient times worthy men and gentlemen have all moved with the times to avoid disaster and harm, the record states. Your brothers' achievement and fame cover the age; you have held power for years — can the court ministers humiliated by your household even be counted? Also the heir apparent, because his wishes are not carried out, constantly gnashes his teeth at those in power, the record states. Though you attach yourself to the ruler, those who wish to endanger you are also many, the record states. If the ruler one day abandons his ministers, where will you find shelter? Now the crown prince has lost the empress's love; the ruler has long had intent to depose him — this you know, the record states. Now if you request installing the Prince of Jin, it is only a word from your worthy elder brother, the record states. If you can thereby at this time establish great merit, the prince will surely inscribe it in marrow and bone — then you escape the peril of an egg piled up and achieve the security of Mount Tai, the record states. Yue agreed and reported again to Su. Su by nature was fierce and dangerous; hearing this he was greatly pleased and clapped his hands, saying, "My wisdom falls far short of this — I rely on you to rouse me." Yue knowing his plan would succeed again told Su, "Now the empress's words — the emperor uses none he rejects; you should seize the opportunity and early attach yourself, then not only will you long preserve rank and emolument but pass the succession to sons and grandsons, the record states. Moreover the Prince of Jin bends his body to honor scholars and his reputation grows daily; personally practicing thrift, he has the bearing of the ruler, the record states. By Yue's reckoning he will surely be able to settle the realm, the record states. If elder brother hesitates, once there is a change and the crown prince holds power, I fear disaster will come within days, the record states. Su then carried out this strategy; the crown prince was indeed deposed.
105
及帝在東都，令約詣京師享廟，行至華陰，見其先墓。 遂枉道拜哭，為憲司所劾，坐免官。 尋拜浙陽太守。 其兄子玄感時為禮部尚書，與約恩義甚篤，既愴分離，形於顏色。 帝謂曰：「公比憂瘁，得非為叔也？ 」玄感再拜流涕曰：「誠如聖旨。 」帝亦思約廢立功，由是征入朝。 未幾卒，以素子玄挺後之。
When the emperor was at the eastern capital he ordered Yue to go to the capital to offer sacrifices at the ancestral temple; traveling to Huayin he saw his ancestors' tombs, the record states. He then left the road to bow and weep and was impeached by the censorate; he sat condemned and was dismissed from office. Soon afterward he was appointed grand administrator of Zheyang. His elder brother's son Xuangan at that time was minister of rites; with Yue his bond of kindness and duty was very deep; grieved at separation, it showed on his face. The emperor said, "You seem more sorrowful than usual — is it not because of your uncle? — so he said." Xuangan bowed again with streaming tears and said, "It is truly as Your Majesty says." The emperor also remembered Yue's merit in deposing the heir and establishing the successor, and therefore summoned him to court, the record states. Before long he was dead; Su's son Xuanting was made his heir.
106
穆字紹叔，暄弟也。 仕魏，華州別駕。 孝武末，弟寬請以澄城縣伯讓穆，詔許之。 終於并州刺史，贈開府儀同三司、華州刺史。
Mu, styled Shaoshu, was Xuan's younger brother. He served Wei as vice administrator of Hua Province. Late in Emperor Xiaowu's reign his younger brother Kuan requested to give Mu the barony of Chengcheng; an edict permitted it. He ended his career as regional inspector of Bingzhou and was posthumously honored as opening general with honors equal to the three excellencies and regional inspector of Huazhou.
107
穆弟儉，字景則。 偉容儀，有才行。 位北雍州刺史，政尚寬惠，夷夏安之。 後從破齊神武于沙苑，封夏陽縣侯，位開府儀同三司、華州刺史。 卒，諡靜。
Mu's younger brother Jian, styled Jingze. Imposing in appearance and bearing, he had talent and conduct, the record states. He was regional inspector of Northern Yong; his government valued generosity and kindness; barbarians and Chinese were all settled. Later he followed in defeating Qi founder Gao Huan at Shaya and was enfeoffed marquis of Xiayang; he held the rank of opening general with honors equal to the three excellencies and regional inspector of Huazhou. When he died his posthumous name was Jing (Calm).
108
子異，字文殊。 美風儀，有器局。 髫齔就學，日誦千言，見者奇之。 九歲丁父憂，哀毀過禮，殆將滅性。 及免喪之後，絕慶吊，閉戶讀書。 數年之間，博涉書記。 周閔帝時，為甯都郡太守，甚有能名，賜爵樂昌縣子，後數以軍功進爵為侯。 隋文帝作相，行濟州事。 及踐阼，拜宗正少卿，加上開府。 蜀王秀之鎮益州也，朝廷盛選綱紀，以異方直，拜益州總管長史，尋遷西南道行台兵部尚書。 後曆宗正卿、刑部尚書，出為吳州總管，甚有能名。 時晉王廣鎮揚州，詔令異每歲一與王相見，評論得失，規諫疑闕。 卒於官。 子虔遜。
His son Yi, styled Wenshu. Fine in bearing and grace, he had capacity and measure, the record states. While still in infancy he went to study; each day he recited a thousand words; those who saw him marveled, the record states. At nine he entered mourning for his father; grief and destruction exceeded ritual and nearly extinguished his life, the record states. After the mourning period ended he ceased congratulations and condolences and closed his door to read books, the record states. Within several years he broadly mastered books and records, the record states. In the time of Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou he was grand administrator of Ningdu, very renowned for ability; he was ennobled baron of Lechang, and later several times for military merit his rank was advanced to marquis. When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister he handled affairs of Jizhou. When he ascended the throne he was appointed vice director of the imperial clan and given upper opening general. When Prince of Shu Xiu garrisoned Yizhou the court greatly selected overseers; because Yi was upright he was appointed chief clerk of the area commander of Yizhou, and soon transferred to minister of war of the Southwest Route Mobile Headquarters. Later he passed through director of the imperial clan and minister of punishments and went out as area commander of Wuzhou, very renowned for ability. At that time the Prince of Jin Guang garrisoned Yangzhou; an edict ordered Yi once each year to meet with the prince, discuss gains and losses, and remonstrate regarding doubts and omissions, the record states. He died while in office. His son was Qianxun.
109
寬子蒙仁，儉弟也。 少有大志，每與諸兒童遊處，必擇高大之物坐之，見者咸異焉。 及長，頗解屬文，尤尚武藝。 弱冠，除奉朝請。 父鈞出鎮恆州，請隨從展效，乃授高闕戍主。 既而蠕蠕亂，共主阿那瑰奔魏，魏帝詔鈞衛送，寬亦從行。 時北邊賊起，攻圍鎮城。 鈞卒，城人等推寬守禦。 尋而城陷，寬乃北走蠕蠕，後討六鎮賊破，寬始得還朝。
Kuan's son Mengren was Jian's younger brother, the record states. From youth he had great ambition; whenever he played with other children he always chose the tallest object to sit on; those who saw him all marveled, the record states. When grown he was fairly skilled at composing prose and especially valued martial arts, the record states. At the capping age he was appointed attendant at court audience. His father Jun went out to garrison Hengzhou and requested to follow and show merit; he was therefore appointed commandant of Gaokai Pass. Before long the Rouran were in disorder; their ruler Anagui fled to Wei; Emperor Wen of Wei ordered Jun to escort and guard him, and Kuan also followed on the journey, the record states. At that time bandits rose on the northern frontier and besieged the garrison city, the record states. Jun died; the people of the city and others pushed Kuan to defend, the record states. Soon afterward the city fell; Kuan fled north to the Rouran; later when the Six Garrisons bandits were defeated Kuan was able to return to court, the record states.
110
廣陽王深與寬素相昵，深犯法得罪，寬被逮捕。 孝莊為侍中，與寬有舊，藏之於宅，遇赦得免。 除宗正丞。 北海王顥少相器重，時為大行臺北征葛榮，欲啟寬為左丞。 寬辭以孝莊厚恩未報，義不見利而動。 顥未之許，顥妹婿李神軌謂顥曰：「匹夫猶不可奪志，況義士乎。 」乃止。
Prince of Guangyang Shen was naturally intimate with Kuan; Shen violated the law and was condemned; Kuan was arrested, the record states. Emperor Xiaozhuang as attendant-in-ordinary had old ties with Kuan and hid him in his residence; meeting an amnesty he escaped punishment, the record states. He was appointed assistant director of the imperial clan. Prince of Beihai Hao from youth greatly valued him; at that time as grand mobile headquarters he marched north to attack Ge Rong and wished to appoint Kuan left assistant. Kuan declined, saying Emperor Xiaozhuang's deep kindness had not been repaid and righteousness did not move for profit, the record states. Hao did not agree; Hao's brother-in-law Li Shengui told Hao, "Even a common man cannot have his resolve broken — how much more a man of righteousness." Then he stopped.
111
孝莊踐阼，累遷洛陽令，以都督從太宰、上党王元穆討平邢杲。 師未還。 屬元顥入洛，莊帝出居河內。 天穆懼，集諸將謀之。 寬勸天穆徑取成皋，會兵伊、洛。 天穆然之，乃趣成皋，令寬與爾硃兆為後拒。 尋以眾議不同，乃回赴石濟。 寬夜行失道，遂後期，諸將咸言寬少與北海周旋，今不來矣。 天穆答曰：「楊寬非輕去就者也，吾當為諸君明之。 」言訖，候騎白寬至。 天穆撫髀而笑曰：「吾固知其必來。 」遽出帳迎，握其手曰：「是所望也」與天穆俱謁孝莊於太行。 仍為都督，從平河內，進圍北中。 時梁陳慶之為顥勒兵守北門，天穆駐馬圍外，遣寬至城下說慶之，不答，久之乃曰：「賢兄撫軍在，頗欲相見不？ 」寬答：「僕兄既力屈凶威，跡淪逆黨，人臣之理，何煩相見。 」天穆聞之，自此彌敬。
When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne Kuan rose in stages to magistrate of Luoyang and as area commander followed Grand Preceptor, Prince of Shangdang Yuan Mu in suppressing and pacifying Xing Gao. The army had not returned yet. When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Emperor Zhuang went out to reside at Henei, the record states. Mu was afraid and gathered the generals to plot, the record states. Kuan urged Mu to go directly to take Chenggao and assemble troops at Yi and Luo, the record states. Mu agreed and therefore hurried to Chenggao, ordering Kuan and Erzhu Zhao to serve as rear guard, the record states. Soon because popular opinion differed they turned back and went to Shiji, the record states. Kuan traveled by night and lost the road, therefore arriving late; the generals all said Kuan in youth had dealings with Beihai and now would not come, the record states. Mu replied, "Yang Kuan is not one to lightly leave or stay; I shall explain this to you all." When he finished speaking, scouts reported Kuan had arrived, the record states. Mu stroked his thigh and laughed, saying, "I knew all along he would come." He immediately went out of the tent to welcome him, grasped his hand and said, "This is what I hoped for," and together with Mu paid respects to Emperor Xiaozhuang at Taihang, the record states. He was again made area commander and followed in pacifying Henei and advancing to besiege Northern Center, the record states. At that time Liang's Chen Qingzhi for Hao mustered troops to guard the north gate; Mu halted his horse outside the encirclement and sent Kuan below the walls to persuade Qingzhi; he did not answer; after a long while he finally said, "Your worthy elder brother the Pacification General is here — do you not wish to meet him? — so he said." Kuan answered, "My elder brother has already exhausted his strength against fierce power and his traces have sunk into the rebel faction — such is the principle of a minister; why trouble to meet." When Mu heard this he from this time respected Kuan ever more, the record states.
112
孝莊反正，除太府卿、華州大中正，封澄城縣伯。 爾硃榮被誅，其從弟世澄等出據河橋，還逼京師，進寬使持節、大都督，隨機捍禦。 世隆謂寬曰：「豈忘大宰相知之深也？ 」寬答曰：「太宰見愛以禮，人臣之交耳，今日之事，事君之節。 」及爾硃兆陷洛陽，囚執孝莊帝，寬還洛不可，遂自成皋奔梁。 至建鄴，聞莊帝弑崩，寬發喪盡禮，梁武義之。 尋而禮送還。 孝武初，除給事黃門侍郎。
When Emperor Xiaozhuang was restored to correctness he was appointed director of the imperial treasury and senior rectifier of Hua Province and enfeoffed baron of Chengcheng. When Erzhu Rong was executed his younger cousin Shicheng and others went out and held Heliang, again pressing the capital; Kuan was advanced and sent as bearer of the staff of authority and grand area commander to resist as circumstances required. Shilong said to Kuan, "Have you forgotten how deeply the Grand Chancellor knew you? — so he said." Kuan answered, "The Grand Preceptor treated me with love through ritual — that is the exchange of minister and subject. Today's affair is the integrity of serving one's ruler." When Erzhu Zhao took Luoyang and imprisoned Emperor Xiaozhuang, Kuan could not return to Luoyang and therefore from Chenggao fled to Liang, the record states. Reaching Jiankang he heard Emperor Zhuang had been murdered; Kuan observed mourning with full ritual; Emperor Wu of Liang commended his righteousness, the record states. Before long he was sent back with full ceremony. At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu he was appointed gentlemen-in-attendance of the yellow gate.
113
孝武與齊神武有隙，遂召募驍勇，廣增宿衛，以寬為閣內大都督，專總禁旅。 從孝武入關，兼吏部尚書，錄從駕勳，進爵華山郡公。 大統初，遷太子太傅。 五年，除驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、都督、東雍州刺史，即本州也。 廢帝初，為尚書左僕射、將作大監，坐事免。 周明帝初，拜大將軍，從駕蘭祥討吐谷渾，破之，別封宜陽縣公。 除小塚宰，轉禦正中大夫。 武成二年，詔寬與麟趾殿學士參定經籍。
Emperor Xiaowu had a rift with Qi founder Gao Huan and therefore recruited fierce warriors and broadly increased palace guard; he made Kuan grand area commander within the gate and exclusively commanded the forbidden troops. Following Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong he was concurrently minister of the Masters of Writing and recorded merit of those who followed the imperial carriage; his rank was advanced to Duke of Huashan. At the beginning of Great Unity he was transferred to junior tutor of the crown prince. In the fifth year he was appointed general of agile cavalry, opening general with honors equal to the three excellencies, area commander, and regional inspector of Eastern Yong — his native province. At the beginning of Emperor Fei he was left vice director of the Masters of Writing and grand supervisor of construction and sat condemned and was dismissed for an offense. At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Zhou he was appointed general-in-chief, followed the emperor on the Lanxiang campaign against Tuyuhun, defeated them, and was separately enfeoffed duke of Yiyang. He was appointed lesser grand regent and transferred to director of the imperial carriages bureau. In the second year of Wucheng an edict ordered Kuan together with scholars of the Linqiu Hall to collate and fix the classics, the record states.
114
寬性通敏，有器幹。 頻牧數州，號稱清簡。 曆居台閣，有當官之譽。 然與柳機不協，案成其罪，時論頗以此譏之。 保定元年，除總管梁興等十九州諸軍事、梁州刺史。 薨于州，贈華、陝、虞、上、潞五州刺史，諡曰元。 子文恩。
Kuan's nature was penetrating and quick, with capacity and backbone, the record states. Repeatedly governing several provinces he was called pure and simple, the record states. Passing through posts at the high offices he had the reputation of fulfilling office, the record states. Yet he was not in harmony with Liu Ji and constructed his guilt; public opinion for this reason fairly criticized him, the record states. In the first year of Baoding he was appointed area commander of the military affairs of the nineteen provinces of Liang and Xing and regional inspector of Liangzhou. He died in the province and was posthumously honored as regional inspector of Hua, Shan, Yu, Shang, and Lu provinces and given the posthumous name Yuan (Primary). His son was Wen'en.
115
文恩字溫才。 在周，年十一，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。 尋以父功，封新豐縣子。 天和初，行武都太守。 十姓獠反，文恩討平之。 復行翼州事。 党項羌叛，文恩又討平之。 進擊資中、武康、隆山等生獠及東山獠，並破之。 從陳王攻齊河陰城，又從武帝攻拔晉州，授上儀同三司，改封承寧縣公。 壽陽劉叔仁作亂，從清河公宇文神舉討之，戰于鹆專井，在陣禽叔仁。 又別從王誼破賊於鯉魚柵。 後累以軍功遷果毅左旅下大夫。
Wen'en, styled Wenzi. In Zhou, at eleven he was appointed general of the cavalry and chariots, honors equal to the three excellencies, and regular cavaliers-attendant. Soon because of his father's merit he was enfeoffed baron of Xinfeng. At the beginning of Tianhe he acted as grand administrator of Wudu. The Ten-Surname Liao rebelled; Wen'en suppressed and pacified them, the record states. He again acted in the affairs of Yizhou. The Tangut Qiang rebelled; Wen'en again suppressed and pacified them, the record states. Advancing he attacked the raw Liao of Zizhong, Wukang, Longshan, and the eastern mountain Liao and broke them all, the record states. Following Prince of Chen in attacking Qi at Heyin city, he again followed Emperor Wu in capturing and taking Jin Province and was appointed upper honors equal to the three excellencies and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Chengning. Shouyang's Liu Shuren rebelled; following Duke of Qinghe Yuwen Shenju he attacked them; fighting at Yuzhuan Well he captured Shuren in the battle line, the record states. He also separately followed Wang Yi in defeating bandits at Carp Barrier, the record states. Later repeatedly for military merit he was transferred to left brigade lower grand master of determination.
116
隋文帝為丞相，從韋孝寬拒尉遲迥于武陟，與行軍總管宇文述擊走其將李俊，遂解懷州圍。 破尉遲惇，平鄴城，皆有功，進授上大將軍，改封洛川縣公，尋拜隆州刺史。 開皇元年，進爵正平郡公。 後為魏州刺史，甚有惠政，及去職，吏人思之，為立碑頌德。 轉冀州刺史。
When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister he followed Wei Xiaokuan in resisting Yuchi Jiong at Wuzhi and with field headquarters commander Yuwen Shu attacked and drove off his general Li Jun, thereby relieving the siege of Huaizhou. He defeated Yuchi Dun, pacified Ye city, all with merit; he was advanced to upper general-in-chief, his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Luochuan, and soon he was appointed regional inspector of Longzhou. In the first year of Kaihuang his rank was advanced to Duke of Zhengping. Later he was regional inspector of Weizhou with very benevolent government; when he left office officials and people missed him and erected a stele praising his virtue. He was transferred to regional inspector of Jizhou.
117
煬帝嗣位，徵為戶部尚書，轉納言，改授右光祿大夫。 從幸江都宮，以足疾，不堪趨奏，復授戶部尚書，位右光祿大夫。 卒官，諡曰定。 初文恩當襲父爵，自以非嫡，遂讓弟紀，當世多之。
When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as minister of revenue, transferred to chief counselor, and changed to appointment as right grand master of splendid happiness. Following the emperor's visit to the Jiangdu Palace, because of foot illness he could not hurry to audience, he was again appointed minister of revenue, holding the rank of right grand master of splendid happiness. He died in office; his posthumous name was Ding (Settled). Initially Wen'en was to inherit his father's rank; considering himself not the legitimate son he therefore yielded to his younger brother Ji; men of the age mostly praised this, the record states.
118
紀字溫范，少剛正，有器局。 在周，襲爵華山郡公。 累遷安州總管長史，將兵迎陳降將王瑗于齊安，與陳將周法尚遇，擊走之，以功進開府。 入為虞部下大夫。 文帝為丞相，改封汾陰縣公。 從梁睿討王謙，以功進授上大將軍。 曆資州刺史、宗正少卿，坐事除名。 後尋復其爵位，拜熊州刺史，改封上明郡公。 除宗正卿，兼給事黃門侍郎，判禮部尚書事。 遷荊州總管。 卒，諡曰恭。
Ji, styled Wenfan, from youth was upright and firm, with capacity and measure. In Zhou he inherited the dukedom of Huashan. Rising in stages to chief clerk of the area commander of An Province, he led troops to welcome Chen's surrendered general Wang Yuan at Qi'an; he met Chen general Zhou Fashang, attacked and drove him off, and for merit was advanced to opening general. He entered court as lower grand master of the parks bureau. When Emperor Wen was chief minister his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Fenyin. Following Liang Rui in attacking Wang Qian he for merit was advanced and appointed upper general-in-chief. He passed through regional inspector of Zizhou and vice director of the imperial clan and sat condemned and was removed from the registers for an offense. Later he soon recovered his rank and enfeoffment and was appointed regional inspector of Xiongzhou; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Shangming. He was appointed director of the imperial clan and concurrently gentlemen-in-attendance of the yellow gate, adjudicating the affairs of minister of rites. He was transferred to area commander of Jingzhou. When he died his posthumous name was Gong (Respectful).
119
論曰：楊播兄弟俱以忠毅謙謹，荷內外之任； 公卿牧守，榮赫累朝，所謂門生故吏遍於天下。 而言色恂恂，出於誠至； 恭德慎行，為世師範，漢之陳紀，門法所不過焉。 後魏以來，一門而已。 諸子秀立，青紫盈庭，積善之慶，蓋有憑也。 及逆胡擅朝，淫刑肆毒，以斯族而遇斯禍，何報施之反哉。 愔雅道風流，早同標緻，公望人物所推。 夫處亂虐之世，當機衡之重，朝有善政，是也。 及寄天下之命，托六尺之孤，旬朔未幾，身亡君辱。 進不能送往事居，觀幾衛主； 退不能保身全名，辭寵招福。 朝廷之釁，既已仗義斷恩； 猜忌之塗，無容推心受亂。 是知變通之術，非所長也。 處道少而輕俠，俶儻不羈； 兼文武之資，包英奇之略，志懷遠大，以功名自許。 屬隋文帝將清六合，委以腹心之寄。 掃妖氛于牛鬥，江海恬波； 摧驍猛于龍庭，匈奴遠遁。 若其夷凶靜亂，功臣莫居其右； 覽其奇策高文，足為一時之傑。 然以智詐自立，不由仁義之道，阿諛時主，高下其心。 營構離宮，陷君於奢侈； 謀廢塚嫡，致國于傾危。 終使宗廟丘墟，市朝霜露，究其禍敗之源，實乃素之由也。 玄感宰相之子，荷恩二世，君之失德，當竭腹心。 未議致身，先圖問鼎，假稱伊、霍之事，將肆莽、卓之心，人神同疾，敗不旋踵。 昆弟就菹醢之誅，先人受焚如之酷，不亦甚乎。 約外示溫柔，內懷狡算，為蛇畫足，終傾國本，俾無遺育，不亦宜哉。 寬閑關夷險，竟以功名自卒。 文恩能以爵讓，其殆仁乎。
The commentators say: The brothers of Yang Bo all bore inner and outer appointments through loyalty, firmness, humility, and caution; as kings, dukes, governors, and administrators they were glorious and eminent through successive courts — what is called having student-disciples and former subordinates spread throughout the realm, the record states. Yet their words and bearing were respectful and sincere, springing from genuine feeling; their respectful virtue and cautious conduct were models for the age — Han's Chen Ji, whose family method they did not surpass, the record states. Since Later Wei, one clan alone, the record states. The sons all stood out excellently; blue and purple filled the court — the blessing of accumulated goodness surely had support, the record states. When rebel chieftains seized the court and torture ran wild, a family like this suffered a fate so cruel that reward and retribution seemed utterly reversed. Yin carried an air of refined elegance from youth and was widely admired as a man of promise. Living in violent times while holding the levers of state, he did help produce sound policies at court. Yet once entrusted with the empire and a young emperor, within weeks he was dead and his sovereign disgraced. He could not, in advance, mourn the dead and serve the living, read the signs, and protect his lord; nor, in retreat, preserve his life and reputation, renounce privilege, and secure safety. The court had already broken faith, and he had cut ties in the name of duty; on a road of mutual suspicion there was no room to give his heart and accept chaos. It shows that flexibility in crisis was not his strong suit. Chudao was rakishly chivalrous from youth, bold and unconstrained; he combined civil and martial talent with daring strategy, aimed high, and measured himself by achievement and fame. When Emperor Wen set out to unify the realm, he placed Su in the innermost circle of trust. He cleared rebellion from the south until rivers and seas were calm; he broke the northern warriors until the Xiongnu fled beyond reach. In pacifying rebels and restoring order, no minister ranked above him; and in bold plans and fine writing he was a towering figure of his age. Yet he built his power on cunning rather than righteousness, flattering the throne and bending his will to the moment. He built lavish detached palaces and led the emperor into excess; he plotted against the legitimate heir and pushed the dynasty toward collapse. In the end the ancestral temples lay in ruins and the capital in desolation — and the root of that catastrophe was Su himself. Xuangan, a prime minister's son favored across two reigns, should have given his utmost when the throne went astray. Instead he moved first to seize power, invoking Yi Yin and Huo Guang while acting like Wang Mang or Dong Zhuo; heaven and men alike reviled him, and ruin came at once. Brothers were torn apart in execution and ancestors burned in disgrace — was the punishment not too severe? Yue seemed gentle outwardly yet schemed within; like adding feet to a snake, he undermined the dynasty and left no line surviving — and that too was fitting. Kuan moved calmly through danger and ended his days with honor intact. Wen'en could yield his inheritance — in that he showed true humanity.
